name: ASCIIText-TS-TW
title: ASCIIText
what_does: Draws a word as a field of monospace glyphs on a WebGL2 canvas, picking each character from an ASCII brightness ramp, so the type reads as a living halftone. It leans in 3D toward the pointer, scrambles glyphs around the cursor, ripples outward on click, and decodes from solid blocks into characters on first paint.
motion: Every frame is one fragment shader: sine waves displace the text plane, the pointer lerps tilt and hue over ~0.3s, a click pushes one of four expanding ripple rings, and an intro decodes glyphs over 1.4s. WebGL2 only — no GSAP, Framer Motion or three.js. Reduced motion freezes the clock and skips the intro but still rasterises frames; without WebGL2 it falls back to a plain text div.
cost: 6 KB gzip of source, no dependencies. One full-screen fragment shader doing a glyph-atlas lookup per pixel at an 8 px cell and DPR up to 2, two textures re-uploaded when the font loads, rAF parked by IntersectionObserver when scrolled out but never idle while visible. Client-only: prerender emits an empty positioned div, the text exists only in `aria-label`, so it must be lazy-loaded and given a sized parent.
fit: no fit. Home's monument wordmark is a drawn SVG (LiveMark); an ASCII raster would replace the one exact mark on the site with a pixel effect, and the pink/orange/yellow ramp is three accents against brass.
reason: a full-screen shader whose only job is making the wordmark less legible.

name: AccordionGallery-TS-TW
title: AccordionGallery
what_does: Lays a set of image panels in one strip; the panel you point at grows to its share of the width while the others compress, its photo drifts against its neighbours, colour returns to it and its caption slides in beside a lit bar. Panels with a link navigate; arrow keys and focus move the open panel too.
motion: A GSAP timeline animates `flexGrow`, `rotateY`/`rotateX`, image translate and a `--ag-gray`/`--ag-dim` CSS pair over 0.6 s `power3.out`; captions fade and slide with a 0.06 s stagger. Triggered by hover, focus, click or arrow keys, recomputed by ResizeObserver. Needs `gsap` core only, no ScrollTrigger. `prefers-reduced-motion` is read once at render and collapses every duration to 0, so it switches instantly rather than animating.
cost: 3 KB gzip of source plus GSAP core (~23 KB gzip). Five panels animating `flex-grow` means layout on every frame of the 0.6 s move — fine at this count, not something to scale to twenty. SSR-safe: no window at module scope, markup prerenders, the matchMedia read is guarded, so no hydration mismatch.
fit: Services › "The five trades" strip. It is already there, hand-ported to `src/components/reactbits/AccordionGallery.tsx` with trade bullets, arrow keys and a reduced-motion branch, without GSAP.
reason: the site already ships a better version of this exact component; the registry build adds GSAP for the same flex-grow.

name: AcidSquares-TS-TW
title: AcidSquares
what_does: Fills the frame with a perspective ground of glossy rounded squares, each tile bulged by a shared height field so the plane rolls in slow waves under two drifting coloured lights. Periodic pulses travel out from the centre, and pointer or click drops ripples into the same field.
motion: A CPU camera with spring-damped yaw and pitch feeds a vertex-displaced mesh (210 × 210 quads, ~88k triangles at default detail) and a fragment shader for gloss, grain and two orbiting lights. Time drives the swell and light orbit; the pointer adds a hover dent and the camera drifts a few degrees. WebGL2 only, no library. Reduced motion renders one static frame and stops the loop, which also parks whenever nothing is settling.
cost: 10 KB gzip, no dependencies. ~88k triangles submitted every frame plus per-pixel lighting, DPR clamped to 2 and the longest side to 2400 px. Client-only: prerenders an empty div and never draws until the effect runs.
fit: no fit. An acid-pink and electric-blue nightclub floor, two accents past brass, competing with the rooms that are supposed to carry the page.
reason: a strong second palette and a surface with no job behind the photography.

name: AeroShards-TS-TW
title: AeroShards
what_does: Streams a ribbon of thick glass shards across five layered depths, with small survey crosses floating between them, edges catching light and a bloom pass over the whole frame. Holding the pointer gathers the shards toward the cursor; clicking sends a ring through the stream.
motion: A WebGPU pipeline built with `vgpu`: 1300 shards across five depth bands following 160-point paths, four bloom levels, depth of field, grain and markers, all recomputed per frame. Time drives travel, roll and twist; the pointer adds parallax and a hold-to-gather spring; clicks emit rings. WebGPU only — `navigator.gpu` is checked and there is no WebGL2 fallback. Reduced motion stops travel, twist and pointer coupling, freezing the field, but the rAF loop keeps ticking.
cost: 21 KB gzip of own source plus the `vgpu` runtime (not counted here), the heaviest thing in this batch: five instanced shard layers, four bloom targets and a full-screen post chain per frame. Client-only: the component renders a bare div and appends its canvas in an effect, so prerender contains nothing. Any browser without WebGPU gets a blank rectangle and an `onError` callback.
fit: no fit. An abstract glass ribbon is atmosphere where the site needs rooms, and a WebGPU-only layer blanks the section on browsers that cannot run it.
reason: the largest payload here, no fallback, decoration with no informational job.

name: AnimatedContent-TS-TW
title: AnimatedContent
what_does: Wraps a block and animates it into place when it enters the viewport: it travels, scales, blurs, rotates or tilts, optionally wiping in through a CSS mask. With `stagger` set it animates each direct child in sequence instead of the wrapper, and it can play on mount or scrub with scroll.
motion: A paused GSAP timeline is played by a ScrollTrigger at `top (1 − threshold)%`, animating transform, filter, opacity and a `--ac-wipe` custom property used by a mask gradient; children stagger. Needs `gsap` plus `ScrollTrigger`, registered at module load. Reduced motion is handled: it un-hides and completes immediately.
cost: 2 KB gzip of source plus GSAP core (~23 KB gzip) and ScrollTrigger (~11 KB gzip), one trigger and timeline per instance. The wrapper ships with `invisible` and is only un-hidden by JS, so a failed or blocked bundle leaves the section blank — precisely the failure the site's own reveal layer is built to survive. Markup is SSR-safe; content is not visible without hydration.
fit: every page's scroll reveal, but that job is already done by `src/lib/useReveal.ts` (IntersectionObserver + CSS, mutation-aware, failsafe-gated) at zero KB. The only idea not already present is the CSS mask wipe.
reason: 34 KB of GSAP to re-implement a reveal layer the site already built more carefully; copy the mask gradient as CSS if the wipe is wanted.

name: AnimatedList-TS-TW
title: AnimatedList
what_does: A scrollable listbox in a padded frosted frame where rows outside the middle half of the viewport shrink, fade and slide off, then spring back as you scroll them in. Hovering or arrowing glides a 1px selection ring to the row and resizes it to that row's height.
motion: Pure CSS transitions plus one hand-written rAF spring for the ring: rows move 12–28px and scale 0.8–0.98 into place on a 620ms `linear()` spring curve, opacity in 300ms. An IntersectionObserver gates the first staggered reveal, then scroll re-runs it against row geometry. Reduced motion swaps everything for a 4px fade and snaps the ring into place.
cost: No animation library; 641 lines / 24 KB of source. `@hugeicons/core-free-icons` is a 6.4 MB barrel — twelve icons tree-shake to a few KB, but the demo items are built at module load, so they only drop if you delete them. One scroll listener, one ResizeObserver, rAF only while the ring travels. Rows render with `opacity: 0` until the layout effect sets a state, so the prerendered HTML is an empty frame.
fit: No fit. The site has no list UI — services are an accordion strip, work is a scroll reel, the contact page holds a form and two addresses. This is a file-manager widget: frosted frame, thin scrollbar, icon tiles, gradient masks.
reason: the gliding ring is forty lines of CSS you can own, and everything around it is app chrome the pages do not have.

name: Antigravity-TS-TW
title: Antigravity
what_does: Scatters a field of small particles in a loose grid, then lifts them into a glowing ring around the cursor where they orbit, banded by travelling waves. Clicking bursts them outward, and when the pointer goes idle an invisible cursor drifts on its own so the ring keeps moving.
motion: The CPU integrates 1500 spring bodies per frame (up to four substeps each) and uploads a per-particle buffer to one instanced WebGL2 draw; a second-order cursor follows the pointer, clicks add a radial impulse, and `autoAnimate` takes over after 2 s idle. No library. Reduced motion scales the clock to 0.3 — it still moves — and the loop runs whenever the canvas is visible.
cost: 8 KB gzip, no dependencies. A 1500-body loop plus a 24 KB attribute upload every frame, blended full-screen; comfortable on desktop, measurable on a low-end phone. Client-only: prerenders an empty div with the canvas filled in after mount.
fit: no fit. A particle halo chasing the cursor is a product-launch gesture, and its coloured glow would sit on top of whatever section adopted it.
reason: decoration that never comes to rest and costs CPU on every frame.

name: Aurora-TS-TW
title: Aurora
what_does: Paints a soft horizontal aurora band across the top or bottom of its container, built from up to three noise-warped layers with a colour ramp interpolated in OKLCH. It brightens and lifts locally toward the pointer and fades in over 2.4 s on mount.
motion: One full-screen fragment shader: simplex noise warps a hem line per layer, the clock advances every frame, and the pointer pulls the hem up within a soft radius on a 0.6 s follow. WebGL2 only, no library. Reduced motion freezes the clock so the band is still, but the rAF loop keeps running while visible; `paused` renders one frame and parks.
cost: 5 KB gzip, no dependencies. Four noise evaluations per layer per pixel, up to three layers, every frame at DPR up to 2 — a full-viewport fill that never idles while on screen. Client-only: prerenders an empty div, so the static HTML and the first paint over FTP carry no band at all.
fit: no fit. A coloured bloom behind the monument wordmark or the closing stage adds a second light source to a page lit by photography, and the stock ramp is the purple-green SaaS aurora.
reason: atmosphere that fights the photograph and keeps the GPU awake for it.

name: Balatro-TS-TW
title: Balatro
what_does: Runs the swirling, high-contrast Balatro paint shader across its container, quantised into visible pixels, with a cursor that stirs the paint through a persistent velocity field and clicks that leave spinning whirlpools. An optional CRT pass adds scanlines and a vignette, and a 2.2 s opening unwinds the swirl into place.
motion: Two shader passes (paint, optional CRT) and a ping-pong RG16F velocity field that records pointer movement and decays; time drives flow and spin, clicks add twirls with a 3.2 s life. WebGL2, no library. Reduced motion still advances at 0.2× — it never freezes — though the loop parks when speed and rotation are zero and nothing is settling.
cost: 7 KB gzip, no dependencies. Device pixels are capped at a 2.4 MP budget, but the paint shader loops five times per pixel by default plus a field pass — the most expensive per-pixel shader in this batch. Client-only: prerenders an empty div.
fit: no fit. A psychedelic card-game shader would put a red and blue swirl behind rooms that are the whole argument.
reason: spectacle with no subject, and reduced motion slows the swirl to a fifth of its pace, cuts its amount, skips the opening and drops the click swirl — it calms rather than stops.

name: Ballpit-TS-TW
title: Ballpit
what_does: Drops a pit of glossy balls into the frame; they fall, collide and pile on the floor under a studio light rig, and the cursor shoves them, drags and throws the grabbed one. A click bursts the pile apart, and the balls can be satin, matte, gloss, frosted or metal.
motion: A CPU physics step (gravity, hashed ball–ball contacts, wall bounce, grab spring) writes screen-space sphere instances that a custom WebGL2 shader raymarches with studio lighting and contact shading — no three.js. Cursor moves push, drag grabs and throws, click bursts. Reduced motion drops the intro fall, drift and burst; the pit still settles, then the loop parks after 0.8 s of quiet.
cost: 11 KB gzip, no dependencies. 200 bodies with hash-grid contacts is modest CPU; the fragment shader does per-pixel sphere lighting over the covered area, resolution capped at DPR 2. Client-only: prerenders an empty div.
fit: no fit. A play pit is a toy; the bar here is a section that carries photography, not a physics demo.
reason: charming, and completely wrong for a fit-out contractor's portfolio.

name: Beams-TS-TW
title: Beams
what_does: Fills its container with glossy ribbons that run at an angle across a near-black ground, each lane lit like brushed metal, and the highlight slides along the beams toward the pointer. An intro sweeps the light source in from below over 1.6 seconds.
motion: Continuous shader time, no animation library: two WebGL2 fragment programs, the first writing a lit height field and the second tonemapping, blooming from mip levels and adding grain and a feathered edge mask. The pointer adds a gaussian light lift, lerped at 7/s; the loop parks itself when the component is offscreen, the tab is hidden or `paused` is set. Reduced motion freezes the clock, skips the intro and ignores the pointer.
cost: No dependencies, about 7 KB gzipped source. Two programs, a full-screen triangle and a float field texture (RGBA8 fallback) capped at 1.6 MP whose mipmaps are regenerated every frame — a real GPU load on integrated graphics and phones, and quality 0.75 is already a compromise. The canvas is inert in markup, so prerender is safe, but there is no static fallback beyond the background colour.
fit: Home, behind the monument wordmark — the only full-bleed slot where an ambient field could sit.
reason: the room reel is the argument; a ribbon field is a second visual language, and in brass it would spend the accent on atmosphere rather than action.

name: BellToggle-TS-TW
title: BellToggle
what_does: A pill toggle whose bell glyph swings when armed, sends out two arcs of ring waves, crossfades one label into another and widens or narrows the pill to fit the new label. It can also carry a count badge that pops in and wobbles when the count rises.
motion: Press-driven. The bell swings through five decaying rotations with the Web Animations API, each pass firing an offset arc; the label clip is a Motion spring on `clip-path`, labels crossfade with a 2px blur, and the badge uses CSS transitions. Reduced motion jumps state with no swing, and keyboard toggles skip the ring.
cost: Only 4 KB gzipped of its own source, but three packages: `motion` for one spring plus both Hugeicons packages for a single bell glyph. If Motion is not already in the shell that is roughly 30 KB gzipped for a toggle. Client-only; it measures both labels with a ResizeObserver and the document-font promise, so server markup is a best guess at width.
fit: No fit — the inquiry form needs a submit, not a notification gimmick, and there is no mailing list to notify.
reason: a ringing-bell joke with two icon packages behind it, on a site that never asks anyone to be notified.

name: BlobCursor-TS-TW
title: BlobCursor
what_does: Replaces the pointer with a liquid-metal blob that lags behind the cursor, stretches into a tapering tail, wobbles at rest, drips droplets when moved fast and bursts into spheres on click. Comes in chrome, jelly, pearl or ink finishes.
motion: Pointer-driven and continuous: a hand-written spring integrator runs a head plus up to sixteen trail bodies, up to 96 instanced droplets and a separate splash body, all drawn through three.js as a raymarched 2D SDF on one full-screen plane with a custom depth material and 2048px VSM shadows. The loop stops after 0.4 seconds of calm. Reduced motion stiffens the springs, stops the idle morph, drip and click burst — but the blob still follows the pointer.
cost: three.js alone is roughly 160 KB gzipped before the `RoomEnvironment` import, against a 150 KB initial budget; the component adds 9 KB of source, an 8-step raymarch over 48 primitive parts per pixel, a PMREM environment and a shadow map. Client-only, fixed overlay, and it removes the cursor from its parent — fatal on a form. `hideCursor=false` is the only sane setting here.
fit: No fit — a chrome cursor is a portfolio toy, not a fit-out contractor's first impression.
reason: three.js blows the entire JS budget and hiding the cursor in an inquiry form is hostile.

name: BlurText-TS-TW
title: BlurText
what_does: A line of text starts out of focus and displaced, then resolves word by word or letter by letter into sharp type. Five flavours: a plain blur, a zoom from 1.4×, a 3D tilt, a focus pull from 0.32 opacity, and a skew drift in from the side.
motion: Framer Motion keyframes per piece, with a spring on transform and an eased filter; an IntersectionObserver at `threshold` 0.1 fires the `view` trigger once, `loop` replays it after `loopDelay`, and `staggerFrom` orders the pieces from start, centre, end or a seeded random. Transforms and filters only. `MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"` is set, so the entrance collapses to an instant state change for those who ask.
cost: 4 KB gzipped of source plus the Motion runtime (about 30 KB gzipped if the shell does not already ship it); one span per word, nested spans per letter, every piece carrying `will-change` and a blur filter during the entrance. Because the initial snapshot is inline, prerendered HTML for `trigger="view"` is blurred and transparent — with JS blocked or slow the heading stays invisible. Put it below the first viewport only.
fit: Services, the five trade headings; About, the opening line of the firm paragraph — one reveal per viewport, never the hero.
reason: keep only the plain `blur` effect at about 6px and 16px of travel, fire once on view, and drop `loop`, `focusOnHover` and the zoom/tilt/drift theatre.

name: BorderGlow-TS-TW
title: BorderGlow
what_does: A card whose 1px border becomes a mesh gradient that lights up only on the arc nearest the pointer, with a matching tint bleeding a few pixels into the fill and a soft bloom outside the edge. With `animated` it runs the same sweep on its own once after mount.
motion: Pointer-driven with no library: every `pointermove` sets React state for angle and edge proximity, which drives two conic-gradient masks and a 13-layer inset/outset box-shadow; opacity eases in over 0.25s and out over 0.75s. `animated` chains four rAF-eased timers for a 4.5-second sweep. There is no reduced-motion check at all — the automatic sweep still runs.
cost: No dependencies, about 3 KB gzipped source. Three stacked absolute layers per card, `mask-composite` with the `-webkit-` fallback, `plus-lighter` blending and a 13-shadow stack; each pointer move re-renders the card and repaints two masked gradients, which is noticeable in a grid of cards. Prerenders fine because the layers start at opacity 0.
fit: No fit — a purple, pink and blue mesh rim introduces two more accents and a soft-light fill that has nothing to say about interiors.
reason: hover decoration with no job, a palette that breaks the one-brass rule, and no reduced-motion path.

name: BounceCards-TS-TW
title: BounceCards
what_does: Deals a handful of square photo cards into an overlapping fan, popping them in one at a time, then springs them apart on hover so the chosen card straightens and rises while its neighbours are pushed aside. Clicking a card gives it a downward kick and fires a callback.
motion: A single hand-written spring integrator on rAF, substepped at 240 Hz, writing `translate3d`/`rotate`/`scale` straight to each card and sleeping when the fan settles. Hover is picked by nearest slot; click adds a velocity impulse. Reduced motion snaps scale to 1, stiffens movement and cancels the pop. No library.
cost: No dependencies, about 3.7 KB gzipped source, one div and one img per card, transforms only. The canvas is a fixed 400×400 by default, so it needs a measured wrapper to be responsive. Cards are authored at `scale(0)` and only revealed by JS — nothing appears without hydration, so the fan cannot be server-rendered content. Hover spread needs a fine pointer; touch gets the click but not the fan-out.
fit: About, the "its trades" section: five cards as material samples that sit fanned on the table and open on hover, each linking into services.
reason: cheap and tactile, but only with 4:5 crops at 300px+, a hairline bone border instead of 5px white, the fan as the resting state, and a static fan for touch.

name: BranchedMenu-TS-TW
title: BranchedMenu
what_does: A vertical menu in which each section folds open to show its children, with thin SVG elbows branching off a trunk to every child. The selected child's branch draws itself in the accent colour while a small marker glides down the trunk to the open section.
motion: Open and close is a CSS `grid-template-rows: 0fr → 1fr` fold; selection animates `stroke-dashoffset` on the branch path and the marker's `top`. No rAF, no library. `motion-reduce` removes the fold and draw transitions; the marker keeps a short opacity fade. Icons render through Hugeicons only when a child supplies one.
cost: About 3 KB gzipped of source plus both Hugeicons packages for eight sample icons — tree-shaken, but a second icon dependency on top of whatever the site already uses. One SVG per open section and a fixed body height derived from `rowHeight × children`, so wrapping labels overflow rather than grow. Client-only open state; the closed menu prerenders cleanly.
fit: Services, a five-trade index with each trade's scope items — but only if the page actually carries a side index.
reason: five flat pages need five links, not a branching tree with icons and a travelling marker.

name: BubbleMenu-TS-TW
title: BubbleMenu
what_does: Puts a floating logo pill and a round hamburger bubble at the top of the page; opening it fills the viewport with giant pill-shaped links that scale up from nothing in a staggered burst, each with its own tilt and hover colour. The close state reverses the same bubbles and fades the labels.
motion: GSAP timelines per bubble on open and close, with a random ±0.05s jitter on each delay; labels rise and fade on a second tween. A resize handler re-applies rotation, and the hamburger lines rotate with plain CSS. No reduced-motion branch. Client-only overlay.
cost: GSAP core, roughly 25 KB gzipped, for a menu CSS could do with transforms; 3 KB of source and an injected `<style>` block. Five large pills plus a full-screen layer, reflowing to one column below 900px. The default hover colours are blue, green, amber, red and violet.
fit: No fit — the brand's nav should be three quiet words in a corner, not a field of pastel bubbles.
reason: GSAP for an overlay, a rainbow of per-item hover colours, and a playful language that fights the dark-luxury world.

name: CRTWarp-TS-TW
title: CRTWarp
what_does: Draws a blocky plasma on a curved CRT: a coarse cell grid with phosphor afterglow, RGB beam scanlines, an aperture mask, bloom, grain, flicker, interference and vignette, plus a power-on intro. Clicking the screen flips to another plasma channel with a rolling, tearing transition.
motion: Self-running, no library: four WebGL2 programs (cell field, glow, separable two-pass blur, display) ping-ponging between two render targets, with a 1.6s power-on intro, a 0.8s channel flip on click and a pointer magnet driven by a damped spring. Time is multiplied by `speed` (0.5 default); `fps` caps the loop, an IntersectionObserver pauses offscreen drawing and it stops rendering after about ninety quiet frames. Reduced motion freezes time, flicker, intro and magnet.
cost: No dependencies and 8.8 KB gzipped source, but the heaviest GPU load here: a full-screen display shader at up to 2× DPR, an 80-column cell field (about 25 rows wide, 45 square) refreshed every frame and a quarter-resolution blur pair. Client-only — the canvas is created inside the effect, so prerender is an empty div with no text and nothing to index.
fit: No fit — a violet CRT is a different brand universe and would sit against every room photograph like a joke.
reason: a very good demo of the wrong world, spending the frame budget on atmosphere.

name: CallChip-TS-TW
title: CallChip
what_does: An interactive status pill for tool execution with an icon, action label, monospace argument, progress fill bar, and elapsed millisecond counter. The fill wipes across during runtime and switches to a green checkmark or shakes horizontally with a red warning on failure.
motion: CSS scaleX transition for progress wipe up to 88% while running and 100% on done, rAF timer updating elapsed milliseconds, Web Animations API keyframes for horizontal shake on error, and CSS translateY icon flip. No GSAP or Framer Motion; reduced motion drops the error shake.
cost: ~12 KB source plus two `@hugeicons` packages; client-only animation logic (rAF, DOMMatrix, Web Animations API), though the base pill markup survives static prerender.
fit: no fit. Monospace argument strings, terminal icons, and millisecond counters belong in developer tooling, not an interior fit-out portfolio.
reason: developer HUD pill for AI tool calls with no relevance to interior fit-out architecture.

name: CardNav-TS-TW
title: CardNav
what_does: A 60px pill bar that springs open into a panel of link cards, the panel's height growing with it. Each card holds a label, one sentence and a short list of links whose arrow swaps for a second arrow on hover.
motion: One rAF spring integrator (k = 160·speed², damping from `bounce`) drives a single progress value; panel height, card translate, scale, rotateX and opacity are all read off it, each card offset by `stagger`. The mount intro is a Web Animations `clip-path` wipe plus a staggered rise of the bar's children; the burger and the Menu/Close word swap are CSS. Reduced motion snaps the spring and skips the intro.
cost: 612 lines / 24 KB, no animation library, but the entire 6.4 MB `@hugeicons/core-free-icons` barrel is imported for one arrow icon. Holds 60px of layout permanently while the panel floats over the page. Keyboard-safe: Escape closes and returns focus, links carry `tabIndex={-1}` while shut. Prerenders as a closed bar; the open height is JS-set, so no-JS shows the bar only.
fit: No fit. Header.tsx opens with a note that the bar must never gain a ground of its own — a slab over a full-bleed photograph is a seam across the picture. This is a floating glass slab, up to 800px wide, over the photograph, and its cards carry the explanatory sentence the site bans.
reason: it replaces a working groundless header with a panel of marketing blurbs.

name: CardSwap-TS-TW
title: CardSwap
what_does: Stacks interactive cards in an angled isometric 3D deck where the front card cycles to the back on a timer or fling. Dragging pulls cards with tilt and bounce physics, while hovering fans the deck out in perspective.
motion: Sub-stepped Verlet spring physics loop running at 240 Hz on rAF, driving `translate3d`, `rotateZ`, `skew`, and opacity directly on card DOM elements; pointer drag with velocity release and hover spread. No external motion libraries; reduced motion disables autoplay and spring smoothing.
cost: 33 KB source; heavy per-frame style manipulation across all visible cards during drag or autoplay; depends on `@hugeicons` packages for default icons. Safe for static prerender, but requires client hydration for interaction.
fit: no fit. A tilted, skewed card deck with fling physics trivializes architectural spaces; ARKRETE's projects page already uses a deliberate vertical scroll stack.
reason: skewed card deck with fling physics demeans room photography and conflicts with the site's calm scroll stack.

name: Carousel-TS-TW
title: Carousel
what_does: Displays a swipeable slide deck supporting five distinct transition effects with pointer dragging, wheel scrolling, and navigation arrows. Slides feature background imagery, title overlays, and an optional autoplay progress bar indicator.
motion: Custom rAF spring loop (stiffness 118, damping 18) updating `transform`, `opacity`, and `zIndex` per slide, plus `scaleX` on progress bars during autoplay. Triggered by pointer drag, wheel, button click, keyboard, or timer. Reduced motion snaps immediately to the target slide without spring physics; no external animation libraries.
cost: 35 KB source code; `@hugeicons` dependency for controls; updates styles across active slide nodes on every frame while moving. Prerenders static slide markup safely, attaching interaction on client mount.
fit: no fit. Arkrete relies on scroll-driven reels and stacks for room photography; interactive sliders with tilt/cube transitions and progress bars add UI noise and break the editorial rhythm.
reason: generic card slider with autoplay bars and 3D transforms adds unnecessary UI widgets over quiet scroll storytelling.

name: ChromaGrid-TS-TW
title: ChromaGrid
what_does: Arranges photography cards in a responsive grid where images appear desaturated and dimmed until a cursor spotlight reveals full color. Hovering also draws an illuminated border and radial color wash matching each card's individual accent.
motion: rAF loop eases pointer coordinates to CSS variables (`--chroma-x`, `--chroma-y`, `--chroma-power`), driving a radial-gradient mask on an overlaid color image layer and accent glow. Reduced motion snaps coordinates instantly without lerp. No external motion libraries.
cost: Zero dependencies, ~15 KB source; requires dual layered image elements per card and continuous CSS mask updates during pointer movement. Safe for static prerender (cards display with initial CSS vars).
fit: no fit. Arkrete treats photography as the argument; draining color from fit-out craft until hovered contradicts the brand, and per-card multicolor accent glows violate the single brass rule.
reason: draining color from fit-out photography until hovered demeans the work, and multicolored borders violate the single brass accent rule.

name: CircularCarousel-TS-TW
title: CircularCarousel
what_does: Renders an interactive ring of images arranged in 3D cylindrical, orbital, or panorama layouts with inertia dragging and click-to-focus. Cards bend along the curve by subdividing their geometry into eight segmented DOM slices.
motion: Custom rAF spring loop (stiffness 118, settle speed 9) calculating 3D rotation, drag momentum, and subtle cursor tilt parallax. Each card's 8 DOM slices receive calculated `translate3d` and `rotateY` transforms. Reduced motion disables intro animations, lerp, and pointer parallax. No external motion libraries.
cost: Zero dependencies, but 38 KB source and extreme DOM footprint (8 slice divs per card × N cards) causing continuous 3D compositing strain. Safe for static prerender but visually flat until hydrated.
fit: no fit. Slicing interior photography into eight faceted DOM strips warps and fragments architectural lines; Arkrete's photography requires undistorted full-bleed presentation.
reason: bending photography via eight sliced DOM strips distorts architectural lines and creates severe compositing overhead.

name: CircularGallery-TS-TW
title: CircularGallery
what_does: Displays an infinitely looping ribbon of curved cards inside a WebGL2 canvas that can be dragged, scrolled, or clicked to expand. Cards distort along an interactive cylindrical bend and sine wave ripple while HTML text labels track them above.
motion: Continuous WebGL2 rAF render loop during movement, passing uniforms for vertex displacement (bend, wave, angle), SDF corner rounding, shadows, and smoothstep edge fading. Triggered by drag, wheel, arrow keys, or auto-scroll. Reduced motion skips intro and disables easing. No external libraries.
cost: Zero npm dependencies, 45 KB source; creates an active WebGL2 context, multiple textures, and instanced mesh geometry; high GPU draw overhead. Client-only canvas (prerenders blank).
fit: no fit. Arkrete showcases rooms through deliberate vertical stacks and horizontal reels; a wavy 3D WebGL ribbon is an experimental distraction that threatens the 150 KB initial JS budget.
reason: 45 KB WebGL ribbon with undulating sine-wave geometry clashes with Arkrete's quiet editorial room reels and strains bundle weight.

name: CircularText-TS-TW
title: CircularText
what_does: Arranges characters of a text string along a circular perimeter and spins continuously like a stamp or seal. Hovering alters the rotation velocity or tilts the ring in 3D perspective, and users can grab and spin it with pointer drag.
motion: Continuous time-based rotation driven by Framer Motion's `frame` loop, using `useMotionValue` and `useSpring` for rotation velocity, scale, and 3D tilt response. Reduced motion stops continuous spin and locks the text statically. Requires Framer Motion.
cost: Requires `motion` (~30 KB gzip) plus 11 KB source; renders individual `<span>` elements per character with absolute positioning and transforms. Safe for prerender (static circle of letters), with motion hooking up on hydration.
fit: no fit. Arkrete mandates sentence case typography throughout and forbids uppercase mono labels or decorative badges; a spinning circular text badge is a dated agency trope.
reason: spinning circular seal requires the heavy motion library for a decorative badge trope that violates Arkrete's typography rules.

name: ClickSpark-TS-TW
title: ClickSpark
what_does: Generates a radial burst of animated particles from the cursor position whenever a user clicks anywhere inside its container. Particles can take the form of lines, streaks, dots, or four-point stars that decelerate, fall with gravity, and fade out.
motion: Imperative 2D canvas rAF loop triggered on click, updating position, length, and alpha per particle over the specified duration. Under reduced motion, spark trajectories are suppressed in favor of a brief stationary fading ring. No external animation libraries.
cost: Zero dependencies, ~16 KB source; mounts a full-bleed absolute `<canvas>` element (pointer-events-none); canvas rAF loop executes only while bursts are active. Fully safe for static prerendering (empty canvas).
fit: no fit. Arkrete is an austere, dark luxury fit-out contractor where photography is the argument; celebratory click sparks or star bursts demean the solemn architectural tone.
reason: celebratory particle sparks upon clicking conflict with Arkrete's dark luxury discipline and austere architectural tone.

name: CodeSlots-TS-TW
title: CodeSlots
what_does: Provides a one-time passcode verification input where individual digits bounce into segmented slot boxes with spring physics. It handles paste events, SMS autofill, horizontal error shake, and a checkmark completion transition.
motion: Framer Motion spring transitions animating vertical bounce on character entry, horizontal shake keyframes on error, and checkmark reveal on success. Reduced motion disables springs and shakes, snapping digits immediately. Requires Framer Motion.
cost: Requires `motion` (~30 KB gzip) and two `@hugeicons` packages (~18 KB source); mounts hidden input layered over animated slot elements. Prerenders static slot containers, but springs and focus handling are client-only.
fit: no fit. Arkrete is an informational portfolio with an inquiry form; the site has no user accounts, client portals, or authentication flows requiring OTP code entry.
reason: OTP passcode verification input has no role on a portfolio site with no user authentication or login flows.

name: ColorBends-TS-TW
title: ColorBends
what_does: Fills its box with a WebGL fragment shader that draws smooth, saturated colour bands which fold and drift like oil on water. Moving the pointer pulls the band field toward the cursor with a lerped parallax.
motion: A continuous `requestAnimationFrame` loop advances `uTime` and eases the pointer uniform every frame; nothing waits for scroll or hover, it is always running while mounted. Needs three.js and a live WebGL context; there is no reduced-motion branch, so it animates even when the user asked it not to (`speed={0}` is the only manual freeze).
cost: three@0.180 is a new dependency on a site that currently ships none of it; a bare renderer plus one shader material is roughly 40–50 KB gzip even after tree-shaking, and the full-screen fragment loop runs at DPR up to 2 forever. One canvas, no DOM churn. Effect-only, so prerender emits an empty div with no height — client-only in practice, and the parent must give it explicit dimensions.
fit: No fit. The only full-bleed surfaces are the home reel and the project photography, and both lose to saturated gradient colour; it also introduces a second colour world beside the single brass accent.
reason: a permanent shader and a rainbow palette for a slot that belongs to photographs.

name: CometDial-TS-TW
title: CometDial
what_does: A circular slider: grab the ring anywhere off-centre and drag or flick, and a lit arc, a head dot and a tapered comet tail chase the value, with the number and unit centred inside. Releasing lets momentum carry the value and a spring settle it back onto the step grid.
motion: Drag, flick and arrow keys all drive a Motion spring whose stiffness and damping are computed from `speed` and `tapBounce`/`flickBounce`; the twelve tail segments re-path only while the value is moving and the RAF parks when it settles. `useReducedMotion` jumps straight to the value with no spring, so it has a calm static version. Requires motion's `animate` and `useMotionValue`.
cost: motion@12 is a new dependency; the `animate` + `useMotionValue` path is roughly 20–25 KB gzip. Twelve extra SVG paths mutated per frame during interaction only, `role="slider"` with full keyboard and ARIA wiring. The ring prerenders, but the centre figure is empty until the first paint effect, so static HTML shows a blank number.
fit: No fit. Nothing on the site is a bounded quantity a visitor would want to dial.
reason: a well-built control looking for a number, and ARKRETE has none.

name: CountUp-TS-TW
title: CountUp
what_does: Counts a figure from one value to another when it scrolls into view, either as plain changing text or as odometer columns where each digit rolls on its own delay. Roll mode adds vertical motion blur and can compress large numbers to K/M/B.
motion: One `animate(0, duration)` tween drives a render callback; roll mode writes `translateY` on digit strips and sets an SVG Gaussian blur from instantaneous speed. Starts once, on view or load; prefers-reduced-motion calls the finish path immediately and shows the final value.
cost: motion@12, roughly 20–25 KB gzip, for what is ultimately a text tween. Roll mode creates a four-cell strip plus a blur filter per digit and a hidden measure row, so a four-digit figure is dozens of nodes. The plain mode server-renders the `from` value, so prerender shows `0` (or the start) until JS runs.
fit: No fit. There is no figure on the site worth counting, and the brief rules out stat rows.
reason: a stat-row part for a site that deliberately has no stats.

name: Counter-TS-TW
title: Counter
what_does: Odometer digits: every decimal place is a vertical strip of 0–9 that rolls to its new value with spring overshoot, staggered right to left, and blurs with speed. Numbers are formatted through `Intl.NumberFormat`, so currency, separators, decimals and non-Latin numerals all work.
motion: A hand-written spring integrator on RAF, per digit, with width interpolation so proportional fonts do not jump and a `feGaussianBlur` whose radius comes from velocity; the intro fires from IntersectionObserver once. Reduced motion zeroes position and blur, and the RAF stops when everything settles — a genuinely calm static state.
cost: Zero dependencies, ~21 KB of source, but heavy DOM for a number: ten absolutely-positioned numerals per digit plus a hidden measure row, a `ResizeObserver` and a `document.fonts.ready` wait. The accessible value is an `sr-only` string, so it degrades to readable text without motion. Client-side measurement makes the visible version effectively client-only.
fit: No fit. It exists to make a figure feel expensive, and the site shows no figures.
reason: the best-built thing in the batch, aimed at a number ARKRETE never displays.

name: Crosshair-TS-TW
title: Crosshair
what_does: Lays a full-viewport crosshair over the page that tracks the pointer on a canvas, tags its x and y in ten-pixel mono, and snaps corner brackets around any link or button it crosses, labelling that element's pixel size. Clicking throws a ring, and it can hide the native cursor entirely.
motion: A 2D canvas loop that runs only while the crosshair is settling: smoothed follow, presence fade, bracket lerp, glitch jitter and click rings. Under reduced motion the follow snaps, the glitch is dropped and pulses are suppressed. No library, no WebGL.
cost: Zero dependencies, ~16 KB source, but it injects a global `cursor: none` rule (applied only while `hideCursor` is on) and mounts a fixed canvas at `z-index: 10000` across the whole document; redraw is full-canvas at DPR up to 2 on each frame. Client-only — prerender produces an empty zero-size canvas.
fit: No fit. Mono coordinate tags and a targeting reticle are a technical register the brand explicitly avoids, and the reticle competes with the brass accent on every page.
reason: a HUD skin, not motion with a job.

name: CrystalizedBall-TS-TW
title: CrystalizedBall
what_does: A single glass sphere in WebGL: a crackling electric rim, coloured strands turning inside it, and twelve to twenty thousand dust particles that swirl toward the cursor. Eight presets (plasma, aurora, nebula, ember, frost, solar, eclipse, abyss) change palette, fill and particle behaviour.
motion: A GPU particle field advanced every frame, with a render-to-texture state pass for pointer stirring, a 2.2 s unfold intro and a 7 s settle. Pauses off-screen through IntersectionObserver and freezes entirely under reduced motion, so a still frame is honest. Needs ogl and WebGL2; no canvas fallback.
cost: ogl@1.0 is a new dependency (~12 KB gzip) plus ~50 KB of component source and four shader passes (field rim, dust, stir, composite); 12k–20k particles with DPR capped by a 4.5-megapixel budget and two float render targets. One canvas, no DOM. Client-only and blank in prerender; on integrated graphics it will keep a laptop fan audible.
fit: No fit. A glowing orb is the decorative second-colour object the brief rules out, and the home hero is a wordmark, not a bauble.
reason: heavy GPU ornament with nothing to say about interiors.

name: Cubes-TS-TW
title: Cubes
what_does: Draws a grid of outlined 3D cubes on a canvas; every cube turns to face the cursor, the ones just swept lean and spin, and clicking pushes a ripple of movement outward. Edges can be solid, dashed, dotted or off.
motion: WebGL2 instanced rendering: per-cube quaternions ease toward the pointer each frame, cursor velocity adds brush spin, and click rings push cubes out and back. A 1.1 s intro unfolds the grid. Reduced motion zeroes the springs and disables `autoAnimate` and ripples, leaving a static lattice.
cost: No dependencies, but ~24 KB of hand-written GLSL, quaternion and projection code the team would own and debug. gridSize 10 is 100 cubes of six quads in one draw call — cheap on GPU, but it needs WebGL2 with no non-WebGL fallback, and prerender emits an empty canvas. Client-only.
fit: No fit. An outlined cube lattice is an agency/tech motif; over interior photography it reads as decoration.
reason: 24 KB of bespoke GL to draw a grid the brand does not need.

name: CursorGrid-TS-TW
title: CursorGrid
what_does: Draws a hairline grid across its box whose cells light up and fade in a radius around the cursor, with line, dash, dot or cross marks and an optional soft fill. Content can sit on top as children.
motion: Pointer position is written into a small state texture each frame and read by the fragment shader, so cells brighten with a smooth falloff and decay over `holdTime`/`fadeDuration`; clicks emit a pulse, `ambient` spawns random cells. The RAF sleeps once nothing is lit. Reduced motion kills the intro, ambient spawns and click pulses.
cost: Zero dependencies but ~23 KB of source and its own WebGL2 context; one state texture and one canvas behind the children, cost is pixel-bound and modest. Client-only, blank in prerender, and nothing renders without WebGL2.
fit: No fit. A drafting grid is a blueprint motif; the site's ground is deliberately empty.
reason: ambient decoration, which the brief rules out by name.

name: CurvedInput-TS-TW
title: CurvedInput
what_does: A single-line input bent along a circular arc: the text, the caret and the submit chip are all drawn on SVG paths that follow the curve, and clicking anywhere on the band drops the caret at the nearest character. A real hidden `<input>` sits underneath so typing, paste and mobile keyboards still behave.
motion: No motion library. The only animation is a 250 ms focus glow behind the band and an SMIL caret blink; text and button respond to hover with a 200 ms brightness filter. Nothing checks prefers-reduced-motion, so the caret blinks regardless.
cost: Zero dependencies, ~20 KB source, SVG paths rebuilt on every resize and measured again after webfonts load. Critically, it renders `null` until a `ResizeObserver` reports a width — so prerender, no-JS and first paint all show an empty form box on the one page whose job is the inquiry.
fit: No fit. Contact is the only form, and its first field is a full inquiry, not a bent email chip.
reason: an arc for its own sake, and it ships blank HTML on the conversion page.

name: CurvedLoop-TS-TW
title: CurvedLoop
what_does: One line of text is set on an SVG path and scrolled along it, so the words bend around an arc, wave, ring or straight rule and loop without a seam. Dragging the line scrubs it by hand and throws it with the pointer's speed.
motion: A requestAnimationFrame loop writes `startOffset` on every `<textPath>`; nothing is CSS-animated. Drag uses pointer capture with a fling that decays, and scroll velocity can feed the loop. Text width is measured via `getComputedTextLength`, re-measured on `fonts.ready` and resize; reduced motion zeroes the speed, and the loop pauses when offscreen.
cost: No dependencies, 15.3 KB source (4.7 KB gzip). The DOM holds one `<text>` copy per repeat needed to cover the path — a circle can run to dozens of copies. The wrapper forces `min-h-screen` and the SVG hard-codes `uppercase`, both of which fight the site. Prerender-safe, but the whole block stays `visibility: hidden` until measurement runs on the client.
fit: No fit. The home already carries the monument wordmark, and a second moving line of uppercase type breaks both the sentence-case rule and the stillness the hero depends on.
reason: moving uppercase marquee with a full-viewport wrapper and no job on the page.

name: DarkVeil-TS-TW
title: DarkVeil
what_does: A slow field of soft light, generated by a small eight-layer pattern shader, drifts across a dark canvas and bends around the cursor. Used as a background layer it reads as a lit silk sheet behind whatever sits on top.
motion: A time uniform drives the shader continuously; pointer movement offsets the field, smoothed over a few frames, and an optional intro unfolds it from black. The scene renders into a low-resolution target and is then composited with sheen, glow and grain. One frame is drawn and the loop stops when paused, offscreen or reduced motion is set.
cost: No dependencies, 27.1 KB source (9.6 KB gzip), two WebGL2 programs plus an intermediate framebuffer. GPU fragment cost runs on every visible frame of whatever page hosts it, which is worst on the home hero; `quality` 0.5 and a DPR cap of 2 keep it manageable. Client-only in practice: the canvas is blank until the effect runs.
fit: Home hero, but only stilled to a near-black brass wash. As shipped it introduces a second light source and a purple default into a page whose wordmark should be the only thing lit.
reason: full-screen GPU ambience that competes with the wordmark and with the photography.

name: DecayCard-TS-TW
title: DecayCard
what_does: A photo card that tears and melts where the pointer moves quickly, then knits itself back together when the hand slows. At rest it drifts and tilts slightly, as if the image were printed on something soft.
motion: Pointer velocity is turned into a simplex-turbulence UV displacement inside a fragment shader; the tear eases back at `recovery` once the pointer slows. The card itself translates and rotates toward the cursor within `travel` and `tilt`, and an idle noise term keeps the surface alive. No trigger other than pointer movement; there is no click or scroll behaviour.
cost: Raw WebGL2, no dependencies, 17.2 KB source (5.7 KB gzip). One window-level `pointermove` listener per card, plus a ResizeObserver and an IntersectionObserver; the rAF loop halves its draw rate once settled. The shader samples a hard-coded 600×750 stage, so any photo that is not 4:5 is cropped. Falls back to a plain `` when WebGL2 is missing.
fit: Projects rooms would be the only home, and there the effect is backwards: it damages the room photography that is the entire argument.
reason: a melt gimmick with a fixed 4:5 stage, applied to the one asset that must stay intact.

name: DecryptedText-TS-TW
title: DecryptedText
what_does: Each character of a line flickers through random glyphs and then settles into the real letter, either all at once, one letter at a time, or outward from a point. The finished line is real text: a hidden copy sits in the DOM for screen readers.
motion: A `setInterval` swaps glyphs from the pool until the mask resolves; substitute glyphs are measured on a canvas and scaled so the line never reflows. `flip` adds a Web Animations rotateX on each cell, `fade` dims the unresolved ones. Triggers on hover, in-view, click, or in-view-then-hover; reduced motion reveals the text instantly and never starts the interval.
cost: Depends on `motion@^12.23.12`, but the only use is a `<motion.span>` wrapper — no motion API is called, so the dependency is dead weight and the file would work as a plain span. 19.8 KB source (5.6 KB gzip); one span per character plus a hidden glyph while scrambled; the interval only runs during a reveal.
fit: No fit. A hacker-style decryption read belongs to a security product, not to a fit-out firm's quiet pages.
reason: a tech demo that ships a full animation library to render a `span`.

name: DepthCarousel-TS-TW
title: DepthCarousel
what_does: A rail of photo cards in 3D: the front card is sharp and full size, and the ones behind step backwards, slide sideways, dim and blur. Drag, wheel or arrow keys move the rail, and it settles on whichever card is nearest.
motion: One GSAP tween animates a float position, and every card's transform, opacity, filter and z-index is rewritten on each frame of that tween; release velocity from a drag is projected into the snap target. Wheel input scrubs the rail and snaps 130 ms after the last event. Autoplay pauses on hover and focus; reduced motion collapses every tween to zero duration.
cost: Pulls in `gsap@^3.13.0` (roughly 25 KB gzip for core) to run one rail. 16 KB source (4.6 KB gzip); every card and every image is mounted and loaded eagerly, with no lazy loading. The wheel listener is non-passive and calls `preventDefault`, so the page cannot be scrolled while the pointer is over it.
fit: Projects, where the brief already calls for a scroll stack of rooms; this would be a second, competing way to move through the same images and would trap the scroll the page depends on.
reason: GSAP for a rail that duplicates the room stack and blocks page scroll.

name: DepthText-TS-TW
title: DepthText
what_does: A word is drawn as 34 stacked copies of itself, each pushed a couple of pixels further back, so it reads as solid extruded type. It leans toward the pointer, drifts on its own when left alone, and grows out of flat type on first paint.
motion: A CSS `perspective` wrapper holds a `preserve-3d` stage; each slice sits at `translateZ(-n × depth)` and the stack's rotateX/rotateY is eased toward the pointer, or swept by the orbit when the pointer is away. A spring sinks the stack on hover and press, and the intro grows the extrusion from zero. Reduced motion returns early: static stack, no listeners, no rAF.
cost: No dependencies, 13.7 KB source (4.0 KB gzip). Default 34 copies of the word are absolutely positioned text nodes, so DOM count scales directly with `layers` — cap it at eight or ten. `autoOrbit` keeps a rAF alive indefinitely; turn it off and the loop parks itself once settled. The real word is in the DOM, so it prerenders and is readable before hydration.
fit: Home, on the monument wordmark: six to ten layers, `depth` near 0.8, `autoOrbit` off, `depthColor` a bone-on-black step, `tilt` under 4.
reason: the only component here that deepens the wordmark without a dependency, once the slice count and the orbit are cut.

name: Dither-TS-TW
title: Dither
what_does: A full-bleed field of slow noise waves rendered as a Bayer, halftone, line or crosshatch dither, in up to eight palette steps. The pointer erases, reveals or ripples the pattern as it crosses the surface.
motion: Two WebGL2 passes: an fbm wave field drawn into a half-resolution framebuffer, then a dither pass sampled at cell resolution. Pointer positions feed a 16-point trail and up to four click ripples that warp the field. The loop stops when idle, offscreen or the tab is hidden; reduced motion freezes the clock but still draws one frame.
cost: No dependencies, 24.8 KB source (7.3 KB gzip): two shader programs and a framebuffer. It fills its parent (`h-full w-full`), so it needs an explicitly sized box, and it adds window-level `pointermove` and `pointerdown` listeners plus a DPR cap of 2. Loses the GL context on unmount. Client-only.
fit: No fit. This is ambient shader behind content; the site's ground should stay a still near-black so the photography is the only texture on the page.
reason: two-pass GPU decoration with no section to carry.

name: DitherVeil-TS-TW
title: DitherVeil
what_does: A photograph is shown as a one-bit duotone dither — ink on paper, Floyd–Steinberg or Atkinson — and a soft circular mask burns through it to the full-colour image under the cursor. The colour lingers behind the pointer and the dither knits back cell by cell.
motion: A WebGL mask pass accumulates a fading trail, and the view shader mixes dithered and full-colour sampling by that mask, with an optional rim and click bursts. `wander` moves the reveal on its own when the pointer leaves. The rAF loop runs only while the pointer is active, a burst is alive, or the intro is playing.
cost: `ogl@^1.0.11` (roughly 20 KB gzip) plus 26.3 KB of source (8.2 KB gzip). Floyd/Atkinson error diffusion runs synchronously on a 2D canvas with `getImageData` whenever the cell size, cover or grading changes — that is the expensive part, not the shader. DPR capped at 2; canvas is injected into a div, so it is client-only.
fit: Projects rooms could carry it, but it shows every room as a dither until touched, which undersells the photography the page exists to display.
reason: ogl plus a CPU diffusion pass to make the rooms look worse than the photographs.

name: Dock-TS-TW
title: Dock
what_does: A macOS dock: a translucent bar of icon tiles that swell as the pointer nears, bounce once when launched, and can carry badges, labels, active dots and multi-level context menus. It parks on any screen edge and can hide until the pointer reaches that edge.
motion: A per-item spring integrator runs inside one rAF and writes width and height, so neighbours grow and shove each other aside in proportion to pointer distance. A click launches a hop, the panel slides on auto-hide, and menus animate in through a portal with an SVG clip path that morphs from the dock tile. Reduced motion is honoured through `motion-reduce` classes and a `reduce` check that disables the spring.
cost: `react-dom@^19.0.0` for `createPortal`, plus 46.3 KB source (11.7 KB gzip) — the heaviest component in this batch. Menus render outside the tree and manage their own focus and keyboard navigation; the rAF only runs while something is moving. ARIA wiring is unusually complete for a demo component.
fit: No fit. A dock is an operating-system metaphor; the site needs a quiet header with five links, not a launcher.
reason: the heaviest file in the batch for a metaphor that belongs to a desktop, not a fit-out firm.

name: DodgeField-TS-TW
title: DodgeField
what_does: A fixed-height field holding one child that slides away from the pointer, further the closer the pointer gets, until it relents after `patience` dodges and lets itself be clicked. A default button cycles taunts ("Catch me", "Nope", "Too slow") and inverts for a moment when caught.
motion: Framer Motion: two motion values in a `useMotionTemplate` translate, retargeted by `animate()` springs on every pointer move — 130ms out, 620ms home with 0.1 bounce. Pointer position is read on `pointermove` and turned into one rAF; a ResizeObserver keeps the field's half-room. Reduced motion pins it at zero; coarse pointers and touch get the still child.
cost: `motion` measures 45 KB gzip for the published package, and `motion.div`, `animate`, `useMotionValue` and `useReducedMotion` are most of what it is. 302 lines / 10 KB. It listens on `window` for pointermove, scroll and blur for the field's whole life, at page level rather than on itself. Prerenders fine — the child is in the markup, the transform starts at zero.
fit: No fit. Every path on this site ends at "Request a proposal"; a button that runs from the client's cursor is the opposite of the firm's job, and the taunts are a startup voice, not a Cairo fit-out contractor's.
reason: 45 KB of Framer Motion for a gag with no page it can live on.

name: DomeGallery-TS-TW
title: DomeGallery
what_does: Projects up to 175 image tiles onto the inside of a sphere, five staggered rows around 35 columns, with a dark blurred rim and grayscale photos. Dragging spins the dome horizontally with inertia; clicking a tile lifts it into a centred enlarged frame over a blurred backdrop.
motion: Drag rotates the sphere and releases into a rAF inertia decay; opening a tile animates it from its dome position to the centre over 300 ms. Nothing moves on hover. There is no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch at all, so reduced-motion users still get the full spin.
cost: `@use-gesture/react` plus its core package, 33 KB of TSX (~8 KB gzipped source) and a runtime `<style>` block. 175 absolutely positioned image tiles under CSS 3D transforms: heavy paint on mobile, and every photo is a separate request. DOM measurement and pointer handling make it client-only; prerender leaves an empty stage.
fit: no fit. Projects already carries the rooms as a scroll stack; a sphere crops the architecture, greys it, and hides the work behind a drag nobody will discover.
reason: the photography is the argument, and this makes it smaller, darker and harder to reach.

name: DotField-TS-TW
title: DotField
what_does: Draws a canvas field of small dots on a grid, hex, spiral or scatter lattice, coloured by a two-stop gradient. A circular lens tracks the cursor and magnifies, pinches or twists the dots inside it, with a soft glow and an optional slow wave.
motion: The lens is pointer-driven and re-renders every frame while it moves, settling when the cursor stops; wave and sparkle are time-driven, and holding the pointer down zooms the field. Everything is a WebGL2 vertex/fragment shader over instanced quads, with no animation library.
cost: no dependencies, 24 KB TSX (~7.7 KB gzipped source). Up to 120k instanced quads under a 9 MP pixel budget, DPR capped at 2; rAF runs only while something moves and the page is visible. Reduced motion freezes time and skips the intro, leaving static dots with the lens still available. Client-only; a browser without WebGL2 shows an empty box.
fit: no fit. It is ground texture, not content; a static CSS or SVG dot pattern costs nothing and stays quieter behind the wordmark.
reason: 8 KB of WebGL for a background no section is asking for.

name: DotGrid-TS-TW
title: DotGrid
what_does: A canvas lattice of dots that spring out of the cursor's way, stretch into capsules along a fast flick, and ripple outward from a click before easing back. Dots near the pointer lighten toward the active colour.
motion: Pointer proximity pushes dots with spring physics; pointer velocity stretches them along the axis of travel; clicks emit a shockwave; an intro bloom settles the grid. WebGL2 instanced quads, no library.
cost: no dependencies, 23 KB TSX (~6.2 KB gzipped source), one program and one instance buffer. rAF runs while dots are moving and idles cheaply. Reduced motion zeroes swell, stretch and shock and skips the intro, leaving a plain static grid. Client-only.
fit: no fit. Jelly physics under a luxury interior site reads as a toy, and no page needs a second interactive surface.
reason: playful cursor physics with no content job and no brass restraint.

name: DriftWall-TS-TW
title: DriftWall
what_does: Builds a tilted perspective wall of image tiles in vertical columns that drift past at slightly different speeds, alternating direction column by column. Hovering a tile lifts and brightens it; the whole plane tilts a little with the pointer.
motion: A rAF loop translates each column track and eases velocity when a column is hovered or the wall is paused; pointer position damps into a small extra tilt; hover lifts one tile. All DOM and CSS 3D transforms, no library.
cost: no dependencies, 13 KB TSX (~4.1 KB gzipped source). Five columns duplicated 2–4 times to cover 1.6× the container height — roughly 30–60 `` tiles, all requested on mount. Reduced motion stops drift and parallax, leaving a still perspective grid. Client-only for measurement.
fit: projects, a full-bleed band under the room stack, at `speed` 10 rather than 42, `dim` 0.25, `grayscale` off, `pauseOnHover` true, and a flat two-row grid when motion is reduced. It would read as breadth after the large rooms, not before them.
reason: cheap and thematically right, but only at a quarter of its shipped speed and without the tilt.

name: EchoText-TS-TW
title: EchoText
what_does: Stacks up to 24 copies of a line behind the real text, each offset along a direction and progressively faded and blurred. The copies lag behind the pointer, bend toward it and settle into a single word; clicking scatters them outward and they spring home.
motion: Each copy is transformed every frame: an entrance ramp on mount, pointer-follow inside `cursorRadius`, an idle drift, or a scroll offset — then a damped return to rest. Click bursts push copies outward on a 1.1 s life. DOM spans and rAF only, no library.
cost: no dependencies, 17 KB TSX (~5.1 KB gzipped source). Up to 25 text spans with `filter: blur()` and `will-change: transform`, which is a lot of GPU layers at display sizes and scales with font size. Reduced motion renders zero echoes, so the text is plain and static. Client-only for the animation; the server output is the text plus copies.
