what_does: A full-bleed canvas draws one or more jagged bolts that crackle, fork and dim on a loop, leaning toward the pointer and striking upward from wherever you click.
motion: Time-driven fragment shader: bolts drift and flicker continuously, the cursor warps the nearest bolt and heats its glow, click sends a strike bolt and a flash. WebGL2 only; no GSAP, Framer Motion or three.js.
cost: ~21 KB source, ~6.5 KB gzip, no dependencies. One full-screen shader at DPR ≤2, up to 4 bolts and 4 strikes, 7–8 octave noise per pixel; rAF stops offscreen, on tab hide, and whenever nothing is moving. Client-only — the canvas is blank on prerender. Reduced motion kills flicker, drift and strikes but still paints a static bolt.
fit: no fit. The home reel is photography; electric blue lightning would introduce a second, theatrical material in a world built on stone and low light.
reason: heavy per-pixel work for decoration that argues with the photography.

name: LineSidebar-TS-TW
title: LineSidebar
what_does: A vertical text list where items near the cursor slide right, warm to the accent colour and grow a tick mark; clicking an item makes it the active one and fires a callback.
motion: Pointer proximity only: one rAF loop eases a `--effect` custom property per item over ~100 ms, and that single value drives colour mix, translateX, tick scale and index opacity. Plain CSS variables and JS; no animation library.
cost: ~7 KB source, ~2.5 KB gzip, no dependencies; a list of text nodes, one rAF that stops as soon as values settle. Prerenders as a static list — all browser reads happen in pointer handlers. Reduced motion is not handled, so the shift would need to be disabled by hand.
fit: services page, a left rail beside the five trades: numerals off, marker in brass, `maxShift` ~10, so it reads as an index rather than a toy.
reason: a real navigation with no dependency; drop the mono numerals, the purple default and the 30 px slide.

name: LineWaves-TS-TW
title: LineWaves
what_does: A canvas fills with ~72 hairline curves flowing in slow waves across a dark ground, a brighter band of light drifting through them; a lens near the cursor bends the lines and a click drops a ripple.
motion: Continuous time-driven shader; the palette cycles through three colours, the cursor drags a displacement lens, click adds a ripple, and an intro sweeps a reveal across the field. WebGL2, one pass, fwidth-based anti-aliased lines.
cost: ~19 KB source, ~5.8 KB gzip, no dependencies; one full-screen shader capped at 2.4 MP, rAF whenever visible. Client-only, blank on prerender. Reduced motion only drops time to quarter speed — it never becomes a still image.
fit: no fit. Fine-line waves behind a form or footer would be texture with no job, and they compete with the photography.
reason: decorative, and its reduced-motion path is a slow animation rather than a calm static frame.

name: LiquidChrome-TS-TW
title: LiquidChrome
what_does: Renders soft ribbons of liquid chrome swirling in a dark pool, lit like a studio product shot; the pointer drags ripples through the surface and tilts the reflection.
motion: Always-on shader: sine-warped ribbon field shaded with a four-tap studio environment, plus a fluid height-field simulation (ping-pong half-float targets, up to 4 steps per frame) that the cursor strokes disturb; view yaw and pitch spring toward the pointer or drift on their own.
cost: ~25 KB source, ~7.3 KB gzip, no dependencies; three WebGL2 programs with float render targets, and the most expensive shading loop in this batch. Without `EXT_color_buffer_float` it silently falls back to the static chrome pass. Client-only; reduced motion slows time and kills the parallax, but keeps animating.
fit: no fit. Liquid chrome is a material study; as a hero it would read as a second brand rather than a room.
reason: costly, and it competes with the photography instead of framing it.

name: LiquidEther-TS-TW
title: LiquidEther
what_does: A GPU fluid solver turns pointer movement into coloured ink that swirls, folds and slowly fades; when nobody is moving, a canned demo path keeps the surface alive.
motion: A real per-frame fluid step — splat, smooth, divergence, 32 Jacobi pressure iterations, project, advect — with pointer velocity as force; the idle demo resumes 1 s after the last input. WebGL2 with half-float targets and a 256 px palette texture.
cost: ~29 KB source, ~7.9 KB gzip, no dependencies; the heaviest component in this batch: seven programs and ~32 texture passes per frame over up to 140 000 cells. Client-only, and it bails out entirely without float render targets. Reduced motion disables the demo, intro and click burst, but pointer dye still moves.
fit: no fit. A multicoloured ink palette is a second accent by definition, and a solver this heavy cannot be justified by a background.
reason: the worst cost-to-meaning ratio in the batch.

name: LogoLoop-TS-TW
title: LogoLoop
what_does: A seamless marquee of logos or custom nodes that can run as a straight line, a wave, an arc or a ring, faded at both edges; items can carry a link, a label or a hover colour, and the track can be dragged.
motion: A JS engine writes `translate3d` and opacity per item on a measured, tripled track: constant drift, hover deceleration, drag inertia, optional scroll boost, tilt or ring projection, and a staggered intro. DOM and transforms only; no library.
cost: ~43 KB source, ~11.8 KB gzip, no dependencies but the list duplicated several times in the DOM and a permanent rAF while visible. Prerenders to a static row, so it degrades sanely; the engine starts after mount. Reduced motion sets speed to zero and skips magnify, leaving a still row.
fit: about page, one muted line of material houses and suppliers under "its trades" — line layout, no bend, no drag.
reason: a real credibility element done without dependencies; use line only, and only if the names are worth showing.

name: MagicBento-TS-TW
title: MagicBento
what_does: A bento grid of feature cards pre-filled with small product visuals — an area chart, a bar chart, a document with a highlighted selection, a moving cursor — plus an edge light that follows the pointer and a click wave across the grid.
motion: Per-card springs for tilt, magnet offset and press scale, a radial border highlight tracking the cursor, a click wave that re-triggers card animations, and optional twinkling particles. DOM, CSS and Canvas 2D; no animation library.
cost: ~59 KB source, ~15.1 KB gzip plus two Hugeicons packages; per-card rAF, one 2D canvas per card when stars are on, and `getAnimations()` replays. Client-only engine; markup prerenders but the visuals depend on JS.
fit: no fit. Its native content is dashboards, metrics and product UI — the stat-row, explanatory register the site rejects.
reason: a SaaS feature grid with charts, for a firm whose argument is rooms.

name: MagicRings-TS-TW
title: MagicRings
what_does: Concentric glowing rings pulse outward from the middle of a canvas, swelling toward the cursor, tilting in parallax, and flaring into extra rings on click.
motion: Continuous: each ring carries its own radius and life, hover springs the centre and scale, click adds up to three expanding bursts. WebGL2 — a glow pass into a float buffer, a compose pass and an instanced 128-segment strip pass.
cost: ~33 KB source, ~9.7 KB gzip, no dependencies; three programs, 15 instanced ring slots at 128 segments each, an FBO for the glow. Client-only, blank without WebGL2. Reduced motion freezes time and drops hover and bursts, which does produce a still frame.
fit: no fit as implemented. The same mark — thin concentric rings in one brass — is a two-path SVG at zero runtime cost.
reason: a full render pipeline for an image SVG draws for free.

name: Magnet-TS-TW
title: Magnet
what_does: Wraps any child in a div that eases toward the cursor once it comes within a padding ring, then springs back to rest; optional tilt and scale ride the same pull.
motion: Pointer-driven spring integrated in up to 120 Hz substeps, written as `translate3d` plus optional perspective and rotate; a module-level registry lets only the nearest magnet engage when `exclusive` is left on. No library, and the rAF stops once the element is at rest.
cost: ~9 KB source, ~2.8 KB gzip, no dependencies; one transform per frame on one element, listeners shared across every instance. Prerenders fine — plain markup, motion starts after mount. Reduced motion disables it completely, and touch pointers are ignored.
fit: contact page, the single brass inquiry action only (submit or the "start a project" mail link), with `maxOffset` ~8 and `tilt` 0.
reason: the cheapest motion in the batch, and it can be confined to the one element meant to invite a click.

name: MagnetLines-TS-TW
title: MagnetLines
what_does: Fills the container with an instanced grid of needle, arrow, or line markers that pivot in unison toward the cursor. A click dispatches an expanding radial ripple wave, while idle springs relax each line back to its resting angle.
motion: Instanced WebGL2 shader pipeline rendered on requestAnimationFrame. Pointer coordinates update the attraction center, lerping spring inertia, stretch, and bounce; clicks trigger a radial shockwave; mounts with an intro wave. WebGL2 only — no GSAP, Framer Motion, or three.js. Reads `prefers-reduced-motion` at mount: the intro, the idle wander, spring stiffness, ripple lag and the click pulse are all dropped, and the rAF loop sleeps whenever the field is stable.
cost: 1,105 lines (~39 KB source), zero dependencies. Uses raw WebGL2 instanced arrays and custom matrix math, rendering hundreds of geometric markers at up to 2× DPR. Client-only: SSR emits an empty container div with an aria-hidden canvas; initializes WebGL context inside useEffect.
fit: no fit. A playful magnetic pointer field is interactive gadgetry suited for a creative tech portfolio; ARKRETE's dark, quiet architectural world demands that photography carries the space without distracting cursor gimmicks.
reason: interactive magnetic compass gimmick that adds decorative noise without supporting architectural spaces.

name: MaskedHeading-TS-TW
title: MaskedHeading
what_does: Renders a large typographic heading whose letter glyphs serve as an SVG clipping mask over an underlying photo or looping video. As the heading scrolls or hovers into view, GSAP reveals the words glyph-by-glyph while the inner media drifts with mouse parallax and ambient motion.
motion: GSAP timeline animates SVG text glyph transforms (`translate`, `scale`, `opacity`, `blur`) on trigger. Pointer move updates CSS transform matrix for parallax and coordinates for the radial mask. An active rAF loop drives ambient sinusoidal media drift. Requires `gsap` core. Reads `prefers-reduced-motion` in two places: the reveal timeline is skipped and the glyphs settle at once, and an autoplaying video is paused.
cost: 703 lines (~23 KB source) plus GSAP (~25 KB gzip). Computes DOM glyph boundaries via `getBoundingClientRect` on resize, recalculating SVG transforms on the main thread alongside a continuous rAF loop. Prerenders static fallback typography via `useIsomorphicLayoutEffect`, but client hydration triggers heavy layout recalculation.
fit: no fit. ARKRETE treats interior photography as the argument, displaying full-bleed spatial views; cutting room photography into letterform silhouettes reduces architectural photography to graphic fill texture, and home's monument wordmark is already an intentional drawn SVG.
reason: clipping room photography into letterforms degrades architectural images and pulls in GSAP for decorative typography.

name: Masonry-TS-TW
title: Masonry
what_does: Lays out photos in an auto-packing multi-column masonry wall that springs into place on mount and reflows dynamically during viewport resize. Cards lift or tilt under the cursor, can be dragged to reorder, and open full-screen within an animated lightbox modal with icon navigation.
motion: Custom JS spring physics running in rAF for layout reflow, entrance staggering, and drag-and-drop tracking. CSS 3D transforms handle hover tilt and lift. Lightbox uses FLIP-style transform interpolation via a React portal. No GSAP or Framer Motion required.
cost: 1,170 lines (~44.5 KB source) plus Hugeicons dependencies. High DOM and scripting cost: every tile is absolutely positioned via JavaScript layout math, measuring images and recalculating spring physics on rAF. Client-only layout calculation: server prerender outputs unmeasured absolute divs that shift on client mount.
fit: no fit. ARKRETE presents projects as a calm, cinematic vertical scroll stack of rooms where each room commands the screen; a dense Pinterest-style multi-column masonry grid with bouncy spring physics and drag-to-reorder cheapens high-end interior spaces into social-media tiles.
reason: multi-column bouncy masonry grid and icon dependencies contradict ARKRETE's calm room-by-room scroll stack.

name: MetaBalls-TS-TW
title: MetaBalls
what_does: Renders liquid organic blobs on a WebGL2 canvas that drift, fuse together with surface tension, and stretch apart when colliding. A cursor-following blob pushes and pulls the field on hover, with interactive springs simulating wobble, stickiness, and click bursts.
motion: WebGL2 fragment shader evaluating implicit distance fields continuously on requestAnimationFrame. CPU physics loop computes body velocities, spring wobble, and particle repulsion each frame. Mousemove updates cursor coordinates with lerped smoothing; click triggers an instantaneous velocity burst. No GSAP or Framer Motion. Runs continuously but it does read `prefers-reduced-motion`: the intro is skipped, though the blobs keep drifting afterwards.
cost: 662 lines (~24 KB source), zero external dependencies. Heavy per-pixel distance evaluation loop in WebGL2 across up to 51 bodies causes substantial GPU fill-rate consumption and mobile battery drain. Client-only: SSR emits an empty container div; WebGL context initializes in useEffect.
fit: no fit. Organic lava-lamp fluid blobs and gooey slime physics belong to experimental creative coding demos; they directly undermine ARKRETE's architectural identity founded on crisp geometric joinery, physical stone, and quiet restraint.
reason: organic lava-lamp shader gimmick that contradicts ARKRETE's architectural geometry and drains GPU fill rate.

name: MetallicPaint-TS-TW
title: MetallicPaint
what_does: Renders liquid chrome reflections and flowing specular ripples across an input logo image or rendered text string via a custom WebGL2 shader. Specular bands warp with simplex noise, edge-bending distortion, and chromatic dispersion, reacting to cursor tilt.
motion: WebGL2 fragment shader evaluating procedural simplex noise, reflection bands, and RGB chromatic shifts in a continuous requestAnimationFrame loop. Mouse movement tilts the reflection normal vector. Mounts with an intro wipe reveal. WebGL2 only — no GSAP or Framer Motion. Reads `prefers-reduced-motion` at mount: the intro wipe is skipped and the shader never advances, so reduced motion gets one still frame.
cost: 836 lines (~30 KB source), zero dependencies. High GPU fragment cost due to multi-tap 3×3 texture sampling for edge blurring, procedural noise, and chromatic aberration passes. Client-only: prerender emits an empty wrapper div; WebGL2 canvas initializes inside useEffect.
fit: no fit. Liquid chrome typography with iridescent rainbow dispersion and constant surface warping is a Y2K/crypto aesthetic that destroys ARKRETE's dark luxury world of bone ink, physical timber, and single brass accent.
reason: liquid chrome shader aesthetic directly clashes with ARKRETE's restrained architectural bone/brass materiality.

name: MicroSlats-TS-TW
title: MicroSlats
what_does: Renders a dense geometric field of rounded miniature slats in perspective that undulate like an ocean swell with glinting highlights. Driven by an underlying multi-pass Navier-Stokes fluid simulation (velocity advection, vorticity curl, divergence, 16-step pressure Poisson solver) interacting with cursor drags.
motion: WebGL via OGL. Runs 7+ render passes per frame (splat, curl, vorticity, divergence, 16 Jacobi pressure iterations, advection, and final scene composite) on requestAnimationFrame. Mouse movements and drags inject fluid impulse splats. No GSAP or Framer Motion. Reads `prefers-reduced-motion`: the wave clock is frozen, the intro jumps to its end, and the pointer and drag splats are disabled.
cost: 1,003 lines (~33 KB source) plus `ogl` (~25 KB gzip). Severe GPU compute load running iterative ping-pong texture solvers and framebuffers every frame. Client-only: mounts OGL canvas inside useEffect; SSR prerender outputs empty container.
fit: no fit. A rolling synthetic sea of purple slats running fluid dynamic equations is purely decorative digital tech art with zero connection to architectural interior fit-outs, while placing heavy demands on mobile GPU and battery budgets.
reason: heavy multi-pass OGL fluid simulation and rolling slat sea that adds unnecessary GPU overhead and clashes with quiet architecture.

name: ModelViewer-TS-TW
title: ModelViewer
what_does: Renders an interactive 3D model (GLTF/GLB, FBX, or OBJ) within an HDR environment stage with contact shadows, auto-framing, drag rotation, and subtle hover/float damping. Provides entrance animations ('rise', 'spin', 'fade') and canvas screenshot capture via an imperative ref handle.
motion: WebGL via Three.js and React Three Fiber. Runs demand-based rendering or continuous rAF during auto-rotation, floating bob, and pointer drag interactions. Honors `prefers-reduced-motion` to disable auto-rotation and floating.
cost: Massive bundle overhead: `three` (~160 KB gzip) + `@react-three/fiber` (~30 KB gzip) + `@react-three/drei` (~25 KB gzip), exceeding the site's entire 150 KB initial JS budget. Requires downloading large external 3D model and HDR environment assets. Client-only: Canvas mounts inside client DOM; SSR renders empty fallback div.
fit: no fit. ARKRETE is an interior contractor whose core premise is physical finished space captured in high-end photography ("Photography is the argument"). 3D CAD/model viewers belong to furniture e-commerce or gaming sites, and the 200+ KB Three.js stack would destroy the site's performance budget.
reason: 200+ KB Three.js dependency and 3D asset pipeline have no place on a site where real photography is the argument.

name: MoltenMetal-TS-TW
title: MoltenMetal
what_does: Renders swirling caustic filament tendrils and glowing liquid-metal ribbons across a full canvas via a WebGL2 shader. As the cursor drags across the screen, it leaves a burning thermal trail of heightened brightness and heat, and clicks produce expanding incendiary flares.
motion: WebGL2 shader on requestAnimationFrame running procedural fbm noise, domain warping, thermal trail decay, and click flare expansions. Mousemove appends points to a decaying heat trail queue. Click triggers time-based flare objects. No GSAP, Framer Motion, or external 3D libraries. Reads `prefers-reduced-motion`: the simulation clock stops, pointer leaning is off and click flares are suppressed, so it renders a still frame.
cost: 649 lines (~22 KB source), zero external dependencies. Heavy per-pixel procedural noise and multi-point trail calculation in WebGL2 fragment shader (high GPU fill-rate cost, mobile battery draw). Client-only: SSR renders placeholder div and canvas, shader initializes in useEffect.
fit: no fit. The caustic incandescent neon lava/plasma aesthetic is diametrically opposed to ARKRETE's palette of near-black ground, bone ink, and quiet architectural materials; fiery trails and click flares are video-game distractions with no editorial purpose.
reason: incandescent caustic lava effect with fiery cursor trails that directly contradicts the dark architectural tone.

name: MorphSlider-TS-TW
title: MorphSlider
what_does: Transitions between gallery images using WebGL displacement shaders (melt, ripple, shear, swirl) combined with chromatic aberration and ambient drift. GSAP drives the transition progress uniform while OGL renders the distorted cross-fading textures onto a canvas quad.
motion: WebGL via OGL combined with GSAP. GSAP tweens `uProgress` from 0 to 1 with `power2.inOut` easing when changing slides; continuous rAF updates ambient drift and pointer uniforms. When `prefers-reduced-motion` is active (`uReduce`), the shader bypasses distortion and performs a plain crossfade.
cost: 793 lines (~25.5 KB source). Heavy dependencies: `ogl` (~25 KB gzip) plus `gsap` (~25 KB gzip) = ~50 KB gzip total (a third of the 150 KB initial JS budget). GPU texture swapping and multi-sampling. Client-only: SSR renders empty container; WebGL canvas attaches in useEffect.
fit: no fit. ARKRETE's presentation relies on a "scroll-driven reel of six rooms" on home and a "scroll stack of rooms" on projects; melting, rippling, or swirling interior architectural photography like liquid plastic distorts and cheapens the craft of the rooms, and costs 50 KB gzip in libraries for a slider.
reason: melting/rippling WebGL distortion deforms architectural photography and costs 50 KB gzip in OGL + GSAP.

name: Noise-TS-TW
title: Noise
what_does: Lays a tiled film-grain texture over whatever sits behind it, with optional dust specks, hairs, drifting scratches, scanlines and a flicker. At low opacity it stops reading as an effect and starts reading as one camera, one stock, one shoot.
motion: the grain tile nudges its background position at `fps` and optionally drops its opacity for a flicker; the dust canvas redraws specks and hairs and ages a couple of drifting scratches. Time is the only trigger — no hover, no scroll. It stops when off-screen (IntersectionObserver) and, under reduced motion, paints once and holds still. Plain DOM plus canvas 2D: no GSAP, no Framer, no WebGL.
cost: 11 KB source, roughly 1.7 KB gzip, zero dependencies. One 256×256 canvas becomes a blob-URL background (allocated once, then reused); the dust canvas only clears itself unless `dust` or `scratches` is above zero. A `mix-blend-mode` layer makes the compositor re-blend everything under it, so mount it section-sized rather than `fixed` on phones. Prerenders safely: it emits a wrapper div and starts in `useEffect`.
fit: Home, the hero plate and the six-room reel: one grain at ~0.06 over all six photographs makes them read as a single shoot instead of six files. Nothing else on the site needs it.
reason: the grain is the one texture this dark world is missing, but drop dust, scratches and scanlines and run it section-sized at 0.06.

name: OptionWheel-TS-TW
title: OptionWheel
what_does: Lays a list of words on a circle at the left or right edge, so the one at the centre sits upright and large while its neighbours curl away, tilt, blur and fade. Wheel, drag or arrow keys spin the wheel to a stop with one item selected.
motion: one rAF eases the wheel position toward its target with frame-rate-independent exponential smoothing, then writes `translate`, `rotate`, `opacity` and `blur()` per row; the loop stops when it settles. Wheel events are captured non-passively and `preventDefault`-ed, with a 140 ms settle after the last event; drag uses pointer capture after 4 px; arrows step by one. Optional audio tick per selection. No libraries.
cost: 12 KB source, ~2 KB gzip, no deps. Twelve absolutely-positioned nodes, each carrying a CSS blur while off-centre — up to twelve blurred layers compositing, which is the real cost on a phone. A non-passive wheel listener that swallows the gesture will fight Lenis on the home page; it also reads `getComputedStyle` during render to get rem size.
fit: no fit. The only option list on the site is the "project type" select in the contact enquiry form, and a full-height curved wheel is the wrong instrument for one step of a five-step form.
reason: a picker for a list we don't have, that takes the wheel away from Lenis.

name: Orb-TS-TW
title: Orb
what_does: Draws a glowing ring of swirling colour that breathes and wobbles, with a bright point orbiting inside it and leaving a trail. The ring leans toward the cursor, brightens as the pointer nears, and pulses outward on click.
motion: everything is one WebGL2 fragment shader: noise-warped radius, rotating colour ramp, an orbiting light with a lag-based trail, echo rings after a click, and a spring that pulls the rim toward the cursor. Time and pointer drive it; the loop sleeps off-screen, on hidden tabs and while `paused`, and reduced motion keeps one static frame with no intro, reach or pulse.
cost: 21 KB source (about 9 KB of it GLSL), ~3 KB gzip, no deps. One full-viewport fragment shader evaluating 3D simplex noise per pixel, at dpr capped to 2 — 1–2 MP of noise every frame, the heaviest per-pixel work in this batch. WebGL2 only: without a context it renders nothing at all. Must be client-only.
fit: no fit. A purple-and-blue glowing orb introduces a second accent to a site whose single accent is brass, and there is no section it would be doing a job in.
reason: decoration with a competing palette and the highest per-pixel cost here.

name: OrbitImages-TS-TW
title: OrbitImages
what_does: Spaces images at even intervals along an SVG path — ellipse by default, also circle, square, rectangle, triangle, star, heart, infinity, wave or a path you supply — and carries them around it forever, enlarging the ones at the front and dimming those behind. Drag to spin it with inertia, click an image to bring it to the front, optionally show the path or put content in the middle.
motion: one rAF advances a lap counter, samples a 720-point lookup table of the path, and writes `translate3d`, `scale`, `opacity` and `z-index` per item; hover eases the speed down, dragging adds a manual offset with inertia, and the intro spreads items out from the front over 1.3 s. SVG plus DOM transforms, no animation library.
cost: 33 KB source, ~4.5 KB gzip, no deps. Builds the LUT with `getTotalLength`/`getPointAtLength` on resize, reads layout rects while dragging, then transforms N images per frame — the images are the real weight. Client-only in practice: before hydration every image sits unsized at the top-left, so reserve an aspect ratio or the box collapses.
fit: no fit. Home already moves six rooms on a scroll-driven reel and projects already stacks rooms; a third device for "rooms in motion" repeats the same idea with a weaker argument, and dragging photographs is a gesture no client asked for.
reason: a well-built toy that duplicates two sections we already have.

name: PaperCrumple-TS-TW
title: PaperCrumple
what_does: Maps a photograph onto a simulated sheet of paper: press and drag and the sheet closes into a wrinkled, creased ball that follows your hand and tilts with the drag; let go and it unfolds back to flat. The print stays on the paper the whole way, with soft stock showing at the torn edges.
motion: pointer hold and drag drive springs from flat to crumpled, with the sheet following the drag and returning to origin; release unfolds on a second spring, or leaves it creased. The crumple itself is precomputed at mount by a position-based-dynamics solve — 64 sampled frames, hinge and edge constraints, layer separation — and played back, so there is no physics at runtime. three.js WebGL scene with a custom depth material for the sheet's own shadow. Reduced motion snaps the springs instead of tweening them and kills the drag tilt.
cost: `three` ^0.180 is roughly 170 KB gzip tree-shaken, more than the entire 150 KB initial budget on its own, plus 45 KB source (~5 KB gzip). Mount runs hundreds of solver passes over a `detail`² grid before the sheet appears — tens to hundreds of milliseconds of blocked main thread — and it needs a WebGL context with shadow maps. Non-negotiable: lazy chunk, client-only guard, static `` as the poster, and a fallback when the context is lost.
fit: no fit. The photography is the argument; crumpling a finished room into a ball of waste paper argues the opposite of what the page is for.
reason: a lovely demo that spends a three.js budget to damage the one asset the site sells.

name: ParticleText-TS-TW
title: ParticleText
what_does: Samples a line of text into a few thousand dots on an offscreen canvas, then animates them from scattered positions into the letterforms. Once formed the word drifts, parts around the cursor, and bursts outward on click before settling back.
motion: canvas 2D, one rAF: the intro eases each particle to its sampled glyph target with a stagger, then idle drift and pointer repel keep it alive, and a click sends a damped spring burst outward. Fonts are awaited before sampling so the word doesn't re-flow after load. Under reduced motion the particles sit at their targets and nothing moves.
cost: 30 KB source, ~3.5 KB gzip, no deps. One canvas drawing thousands of 1-pixel fills per frame, bucketed into 96 tone/fade groups to avoid per-particle state changes; the glyph sampling re-runs only when text, size, weight or density changes. Client-only (needs canvas metrics and `document.fonts`).
fit: the 404 page only: the monument line reassembling out of dust, in bone, with no highlight colour. Not the home wordmark — the mark is the argument's first beat and should be still.
reason: worth exactly one lazy use on the 404 with `highlightColor` set to bone and `idleDrift` at 0.

name: Particles-TS-TW
title: Particles
what_does: Fills a box with a slow 3D cloud of glowing dots that drift and twinkle in a dark space, optionally strung together with faint constellation lines. The pointer parallaxes, repels or attracts the field, and a click sends a shockwave ring through it.
motion: WebGL2 instanced quads. Each frame the CPU advances the rotation, drift and pointer state and projects the first 900 dots for the connection pass, while the vertex shader places and sizes every instance from the same uniforms and the fragment shader draws the glyph with a halo; rotation, twinkle, drift, intro reveal and click bursts are time- or pointer-driven. Sleeps off-screen and on hidden tabs, freezes under reduced motion.
cost: 34 KB source, ~4 KB gzip, no deps. Two GLSL programs, up to 20 000 instances, an optional bucketed proximity pass emitting at most 9 000 line segments, dpr capped at 2. Client-only: WebGL2 or nothing. The 200-dot default is cheap; the ceiling is not.
fit: no fit. A starfield with constellation lines is the visual language of software, not of rooms; there is no section where it would be more than atmosphere.
reason: generic tech ambience, and the site's atmosphere comes from photographs.

name: PatternWaves-TS-TW
title: PatternWaves
what_does: Fills a box with a grid of dots, dashes, plus marks or ASCII glyphs whose size and brightness follow a moving height field, so the surface reads as silk, swell or pond water lit from one side. Moving the cursor drops ripples into it; the presets are silk, ocean, pond, lines, terminal and mesh.
motion: three WebGL passes per frame: a height/normal field, a half-float ping-pong ripple simulation (1/8 resolution, 60 Hz, damped), and a mark pass drawing instanced dots or glyphs from a generated atlas; pointer movement injects impulses. Time-driven; reduced motion freezes time and removes ripples but keeps the surface.
cost: `ogl` ^1.0.11 (~15 KB gzip) plus 31 KB source (~3.5 KB gzip). Dpr is clamped by a 4.5 MP pixel budget, the grid is capped at 4096×4096 cells, and ripples need `EXT_color_buffer_float` — without it the surface still draws, without ripples. WebGL2 only, and it appends its own canvas, so it must be client-only and given an explicit height.
fit: no fit. It would be a third procedural surface competing with the photographs and with the ceiling assembly already drawn in CSS on services.
reason: a beautiful texture with no job, bought with a WebGL dependency and three passes a frame.

name: PeekRating-TS-TW
title: PeekRating
what_does: A row of five stars, hearts or bolts where hovering lifts the stars up to the cursor in a travelling wave, magnifies the one under the pointer and previews the score. Clicking commits it with a pop, a second click clears, and an optional tooltip names the level.
motion: CSS only: `transform` over 320 ms on the hover wave, colour over 160 ms, and a scale pop on commit. State lives in refs with direct style writes — no rAF, no library. Reduced motion drops the lift, the magnify and the pop and just changes colour.
cost: two Hugeicons packages, of which only the three used glyphs are bundled (roughly 6–8 KB gzip); 13 KB source, ~1.8 KB gzip. Five buttons, no timers, no canvas. It calls `useLayoutEffect` to place the tooltip, so prerender needs the isomorphic-hook swap or React's SSR warning.
fit: no fit. Nothing on the site is rated, and the default gold star is exactly the second accent the brief forbids; the enquiry form asks for a project, not a score.
reason: a rating control for a site that has nothing to rate.

name: PillNav-TS-TW
title: PillNav
what_does: A floating navigation pill bar with an optional circular logo, text links, and an indicator dot or highlight pill that glides between items. On narrow viewports it collapses into a circular toggle that unfolds an absolute vertical sheet menu.
motion: A custom requestAnimationFrame spring integrator drives horizontal translation, width stretching, and press squash for the glide pill and active dot; CSS transitions handle radial fill bubbles and burger-to-cross line rotation. Triggered on hover, focus, press, and click without GSAP or Framer Motion. Reduced motion disables transitions and snaps spring states directly.
cost: 37.3 KB source (~5.2 KB gzip), zero dependencies. Modest DOM footprint with an inverted ink text clip layer and mobile panel overlay. Prerenders cleanly with initial active styles, though track measurement and spring physics run on the client.
fit: No fit. ARKRETE's header avoids a floating slab over full-bleed photography, and the site keeps desktop navigation as a quiet typographic row rather than an animated SaaS pill dock.
reason: floating pill bar with bouncy spring physics and mobile sheet that violates ARKRETE's groundless header rule.

name: PixelBlast-TS-TW
title: PixelBlast
what_does: A full-bleed WebGL2 grid of retro pixel glyphs that drift and undulate across the viewport driven by 3D fractional Brownian motion noise. Clicks emit expanding circular shockwave rings and pointer movement leaves a diffusing brush trail across the matrix.
motion: Multi-pass WebGL2 shader pipeline using ping-pong framebuffers for cellular simulation and ripple decay. RequestAnimationFrame advances time for noise drift, decays up to ten concurrent click ripples, and diffuses pointer brush marks; reduced motion freezes simulation time.
cost: 34.5 KB source (~6.1 KB gzip), zero dependencies. Single `<canvas>` DOM element, but continuous GPU load running multi-pass shader simulations every frame. Client-only; prerender outputs a blank container.
fit: No fit. 8-bit arcade pixel glyphs and shockwave ripples conflict with the dark luxury aesthetic and compete with architectural photography.
reason: retro pixel simulation and click shockwaves that clash with quiet luxury interior imagery.

name: PixelCard-TS-TW
title: PixelCard
what_does: A card container backed by an HTML5 2D canvas that renders an animated field of shimmering pixel glyphs. Hovering or focusing sweeps a radial spotlight across the card that scatters sparkling squares, circles, or diamonds.
motion: An HTML5 2D canvas requestAnimationFrame loop iterating over Float32Array typed arrays for particle positions, phase, and jitter. Hover updates spotlight focus, clicks trigger radial shockwave pulses, and time modulates sparkle phase; reduced motion halts the loop and draws a static state.
cost: 23.7 KB source (~4.5 KB gzip), zero dependencies. One `<canvas>` element inside a card container. Canvas 2D CPU drawing loop running continuously on hover, compounding cost across multiple cards. Children prerender on the server, but the canvas background is client-only.
fit: No fit. Shimmering pixel sparkle cards read as crypto or gaming UI, disrupting the presentation of high-end physical materials and rooms.
reason: gaming/crypto pixel glitter card background that adds CPU drawing loops to portfolio cards.

name: PixelSnow-TS-TW
title: PixelSnow
what_does: A WebGL2 canvas effect of falling pixel-art snowflakes that drift downward with wind sway and depth parallax. Flakes repel away from the pointer and can settle into a dithered snow pile along the bottom edge of the container.
motion: WebGL2 instanced sprite rendering with offscreen accumulation textures. CPU advances flake positions, wind sway, and pointer repulsion each RAF frame, while shaders unpack 2D sprite atlases and Bayer dither patterns; reduced motion freezes flake motion.
cost: 32.9 KB source (~5.9 KB gzip), zero dependencies. Single `<canvas>` DOM element. Multi-pass WebGL2 pipeline with framebuffers, sprite atlas uploads, and per-frame CPU particle simulation. Client-only; blank on static prerender.
fit: No fit. Pixel snowfall is a seasonal novelty completely out of place for an interior fit-out contractor operating in Cairo and Dubai.
reason: novelty pixel snow simulation irrelevant to high-end desert interior fit-out.

name: PixelSwap-TS-TW
title: PixelSwap
what_does: Transitions between two content layers using an animated mosaic mask of scaling and rotating pixel tiles. The transition sweeps across the surface in waves following pointer location, center-out, spiral, or directional patterns.
motion: A custom second-order spring integrator running in requestAnimationFrame calculates per-tile scale and rotation. On every frame, it constructs an SVG path string containing hundreds of polygon paths and updates `layer.style.clipPath = path('...')`. Reduced motion skips the spring loop and toggles layer visibility instantly.
cost: 16.5 KB source (~3.6 KB gzip), zero dependencies. Three DOM elements, but heavy CPU cost formatting and parsing massive SVG path strings for up to 600 tiles on every animation frame. Content prerenders on server, but clip-path animation is client-only.
fit: No fit. Novelty mosaic pixel dissolves and spinning square wipes degrade architectural photography and look like video game transitions.
reason: arcade mosaic wipe that burns CPU generating giant clip-path strings and ruins architectural photography.

name: PixelTrail-TS-TW
title: PixelTrail
what_does: An interactive WebGL2 canvas overlay that leaves a glowing trail of pixel tiles behind the cursor. Pixels dissolve through fading, shrinking, or Bayer matrix dithering, with optional fluid gravity flow and specular surface lighting.
motion: WebGL2 fragment shader sampling a 512×512 trail history texture updated every frame via CPU pointer interpolation. Continuous RAF loop advances trail decay, physics flow, and sparkling noise, with multi-tap convolution passes for gooey blending. Has no reduced-motion fallback and runs continuously while pointer moves.
cost: 26.0 KB source (~4.8 KB gzip), zero dependencies. Single `<canvas>` DOM element. Heavy GPU fragment shader with 49-tap convolution loops and per-frame CPU point buffer allocations. Client-only; blank on static prerender.
fit: No fit. An interactive cursor trail of sparkling, gooey pixels is a toy interaction that distracts from portfolio imagery and lacks reduced-motion support.
reason: cursor toy with 49-tap WebGL2 convolution loops and no reduced-motion fallback.

name: PixelTransition-TS-TW
title: PixelTransition
what_does: Switches between two content layers by drawing a 2D canvas overlay of solid pixel blocks that pop or grow to cover the screen, swaps the underlying layer at the midpoint, and uncovers the new content. Patterns include random noise, ordered dithering, radial ripples, and directional wipes.
motion: An HTML5 Canvas 2D requestAnimationFrame loop that draws Path2D rectangles or arcs for each grid cell across two phases (sealing then unsealing). Triggered by pointer hover or click. If prefers-reduced-motion is detected, it skips the canvas draw and swaps layer visibility immediately.
cost: 15.4 KB source (~3.3 KB gzip), zero dependencies. Two DOM content containers plus one `<canvas>` overlay. Idle when resting with zero CPU cost, but consumes CPU during active wipes drawing hundreds of Path2D paths per frame. First layer prerenders cleanly on server.
fit: No fit. An 8-bit blocky pixel curtain wipe between photographs or cards contradicts ARKRETE's refined architectural atmosphere.
reason: blocky retro pixel wipe that conflicts with ARKRETE's refined architectural photography.

name: Plasma-TS-TW
title: Plasma
what_does: A full-bleed WebGL2 background of a twisting, glowing volumetric plasma fluid that writhes in 3D space. The camera subtly tilts and orbits with pointer movement, leaving localized thermal glow spots across the fluid field.
motion: Dual-pass WebGL2 raymarching pipeline: a volume shader marches 60 steps per pixel through an implicit mathematical surface, followed by a composite shader applying tonemapping, specular response, and dither grain. Continuous time drives animation. Pauses when scrolled out of view and freezes on prefers-reduced-motion.
cost: 18.5 KB source (~3.8 KB gzip), zero dependencies. Single `<canvas>` DOM element. Very heavy GPU workload: 60 raymarching steps per pixel every frame, stressing integrated GPUs. Client-only; blank on static prerender.
fit: No fit. A sci-fi glowing plasma cloud is completely antithetical to physical fit-out craft and real architectural finishes like stone, oak, and brass.
reason: heavy 60-step volumetric raymarching shader with sci-fi aesthetics alien to physical fit-out craft.

name: PlasmaWave-TS-TW
title: PlasmaWave
what_does: A WebGL2 shader of two neon laser ribbons that twist, bend, and undulate through 3D space with an intense HDR glow. Moving the pointer bulges and warps the ribbons through a virtual heat-lens distortion.
motion: Multi-pass WebGL2 pipeline using coarse and fine raymarching passes followed by a 3-level bloom pyramid (downsample and upsample blur passes) and composite pass. Continuous time-based sinusoidal oscillation. Pauses when offscreen and freezes on prefers-reduced-motion.
cost: 24.5 KB source (~4.5 KB gzip), zero dependencies. Single `<canvas>` DOM element. Substantial GPU load with multiple offscreen framebuffers, adaptive raymarching, and bloom pyramid passes every frame. Client-only; blank on static prerender.
fit: No fit. Glowing neon light tubes and laser bloom belong to nightlife and electronic music visuals, not a quiet Cairo and Dubai fit-out firm.
reason: multi-pass raymarching and bloom pipeline drawing neon laser ribbons that clash with architectural finishes.

name: Prism-TS-TW
title: Prism
what_does: Paints a full-bleed canvas of a slowly turning glass pyramid that refracts a spectral gradient, with a 1.4 s intro and a faint pointer-follow tilt. `colors` replaces the built-in spectrum with up to eight of your own stops.
motion: Shader time drives the rotation and the colour travel; pointer position adds yaw and pitch through spring inertia; `prefers-reduced-motion` freezes time and skips the intro; rAF stops when the canvas leaves the viewport or the tab hides. Needs WebGL2 only — no three.js, no GSAP, no Framer Motion.
cost: Zero dependencies, about 5.4 KB gzip of source. One full-screen fragment shader running a 100-step raymarch per pixel at half resolution with DPR capped at 2, so it is fill-rate bound: fine in a 700×500 panel, expensive full-bleed on a 4K screen. Prerenders as an empty `<div><canvas>` so SSR is safe, but it is blank without WebGL2 and only paints after hydration.
fit: No fit. A spectral prism behind the home monument wordmark would add a second accent, and a brass-tinted variant is still a per-pixel raymarch buying a glow the existing gradients already draw.
reason: heavy fragment work for decoration that competes with the wordmark.

name: PrismaticBurst-TS-TW
title: PrismaticBurst
what_does: Fires a fan of straight light rays out of the centre, coloured along a gradient and bloomed through four blur levels so it reads as a prismatic starburst. It leans toward the pointer and sends a ring of light outward on click.
motion: Constant ray rotation plus a damped lean toward the cursor and a click-driven pulse that expands and fades; a four-level bloom chain runs every frame. Reduced motion stops the rotation, the lean and the burst. WebGL2, no three.js.
cost: No npm dependencies, about 9 KB gzip of source. The scene renders to an offscreen target at 70 % resolution (`quality: 'high'`, or `resolution`), followed by four downsample/blur/upsample passes at DPR ≤ 2, with an adaptive governor that lowers scale when frames run long. Client-only; without WebGL2 the box stays empty.
fit: No fit. A starburst is a second accent with no job on any of the five pages, and click-to-burst is a demo gesture rather than an inquiry.
reason: four-pass bloom for a decoration this brand cannot use.

name: ProfileCard-TS-TW
title: ProfileCard
what_does: Draws a 340 px ID-style card with avatar, name, title, handle, a coloured status dot and a Contact button on a dark metal frame. Moving the pointer tilts the card while a rainbow foil, a diagonal bar pattern and a glare patch slide across its face, like a holographic trading card.
motion: A spring rAF loop chases the pointer and writes a dozen CSS custom properties, so tilt, foil band, highlight and shadow are plain CSS transforms reading those variables. Touch drag works and `enableMobileTilt` adds deviceorientation (with permission on iOS). Reduced motion zeroes tilt and parallax; no canvas, no animation library.
cost: Two Hugeicons packages the site does not currently use (only the mail glyph is referenced). About 6.1 KB gzip of source, one rAF while the cursor moves, no images beyond the avatar. SSR-safe: markup prerenders, the effect only attaches listeners.
fit: No fit. It is a product-page contact card; the about page is the firm and its trades, and rainbow foil breaks the one-accent rule outright.
reason: a trading-card gimmick, not a surface this site needs.

name: PromptBar-TS-TW
title: PromptBar
what_does: A chat composer: a textarea that grows to five rows, an `@` menu of sources (files, web search, sales data, mail, calendar), a `/` command menu, a model picker with five effort steps, and attach, mic and send buttons. Send morphs into a stop square, and a spark fountain fires when the field is full.
motion: Framer Motion (`motion/react`) animates the panel morph, the send glyph squashing from arrow to square with a tilt, menu entrances and the effort slider; the textarea height is measured and animated; a 2D canvas draws the sparks. `useReducedMotion` collapses every duration to zero.
cost: `motion` is a new dependency at roughly 34 KB gzip, plus two Hugeicons packages, plus about 8.9 KB gzip of component source — close to a third of the 150 KB budget for one control. Text measurement, menu state and a canvas keep it busy, and it prerenders only as a static shell.
fit: No fit. The contact page is a named-field inquiry form ("Send us the drawings"), not a prompt box, and none of the AI affordances mean anything to a fit-out client.
reason: an entire AI chat product compressed into a control the site has no use for.

name: PulseHeart-TS-TW
title: PulseHeart
what_does: A pill-shaped like button: on click the icon shrinks to a dot, flips from grey outline to filled colour, springs back with a beat, and the count digit rolls to its new value. Heart, star and thumb glyphs ship with it.
motion: Click-triggered only: an rAF timeline scales the glyph down to `dotSize` and back with a back-out overshoot, compresses the pill by `beat` percent, and flips `data-liked` at the midpoint so the colour transition lands with the pop; the changed digit rolls on a CSS transform. Keyboard activation skips the animation, and reduced motion commits instantly.
cost: One icon package for three glyphs, about 3.8 KB gzip of source, a handful of spans, no canvas. SSR-safe; the button prerenders with `aria-pressed`, a disabled state and an sr-only label.
fit: No fit. Nothing on the site is liked or counted, and a like pill would put the only number on a page that deliberately has no stat rows.
reason: a social gesture with no place in an inquiry-driven site.

name: Radar-TS-TW
title: Radar
what_does: Renders a radar scope: concentric rings, up to twelve spokes, tick marks, a beam that sweeps around leaving a phosphor afterglow, and up to sixteen contacts that drift, brighten as the beam crosses them and leave fading echoes. The whole plane tilts toward the pointer.
motion: Time-driven sweep or pulse rings, contact drift with heading and turn, sprite halos and a five-level bloom chain every frame; pointer position tilts the plane; `prefers-reduced-motion` stops the sweep, the contacts and the tilt. WebGL2, no three.js.
cost: No dependencies, about 10.1 KB gzip of source. Two offscreen passes plus five downsample/upsample bloom levels at DPR ≤ 2, sixteen sprite quads, float buffers when `EXT_color_buffer_float` exists. Client-only, blank without WebGL2, and the container needs an explicit height or it collapses.
fit: No fit. A surveillance scope is the wrong metaphor for fit-out work, and no section of home, projects, services, about or contact is a live display.
reason: a well-built toy that says security operations, not interiors.

name: RefineFrame-TS-TW
title: RefineFrame
what_does: Wraps an image in a fixed-aspect frame and steps it through four stages: a blocky mosaic sharpens level by level down to the crisp photograph, with a soft feathered seam and a light sweep crossing the frame as it resolves. A chip reads Queued / Generating / Refining / Ready, and the error stage offers Retry.
motion: Status-driven: an rAF loop advances a progress value and redraws a 2D canvas from nine downsampled copies, with a feathered seam and the glint bar; the wrapper cross-fades blur, saturation and scale through a CSS transition. Reduced motion jumps straight to the sharp frame. No GSAP, no Framer Motion.
cost: Two Hugeicons packages for four chip glyphs, about 4.5 KB gzip of source. Nine full-size offscreen canvases are built per resize (48 px to 1 px pyramid), which is a few MB at the default 320 px but hundreds of MB full-bleed at DPR 2 — cap the width or force DPR 1. One rAF burst per stage change, none once resolved. The frame is CSS so it prerenders; only the canvas paint needs the client.
fit: Projects page grid and the home reel panels: keep the mosaic-to-sharp resolve, drop the chip and the generation wording, and drive `status` from the image's `onLoad` over the existing `Img` component.
reason: the one piece here with a real job: a photograph arriving without a flash of empty frame.

name: ReflectiveCard-TS-TW
title: ReflectiveCard
what_does: A 320×500 metal ID card whose surface is a live WebGL reflection of a looping video or the visitor's webcam, blurred, warped and tinted like brushed steel, with glare that moves as the card tilts. Name, role, badge, status, an ID number and a fingerprint tile sit on top.
motion: Drag or pointer motion feeds rotateX/rotateY into a per-frame shader that samples the video texture, warps and blurs it and adds a moving specular highlight; an intro lifts the card into place; reduced motion drops the tilt and refuses to autoplay the clip.
cost: Two Hugeicons packages, about 11.6 KB gzip of source. A hidden `<video>` kept playing plus a per-frame texture upload and a multi-pass blur — real GPU and battery cost — and `webcam` triggers a permission prompt before anything appears. Client-only; no SSR value beyond the printed text.
fit: No fit. An ID badge that mirrors the visitor is a portfolio trick, camera access on a contractor's site is a bounce, and the card chrome duplicates nothing the site needs.
reason: camera permission and per-frame video upload for a demo object.

name: Ribbons-TS-TW
title: Ribbons
what_does: Three coloured ribbons trail the cursor across a transparent canvas, each a fifty-point spring chain drawn as a tapered strip in lens, comet or even width profiles, with an optional travelling wave along its length.
motion: Pointer-driven spring physics integrated at a fixed 120 Hz step, then each spine expanded into a GPU triangle strip with soft edges; it only draws while the pointer moves or the canvas is visible. WebGL2. There is no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch at all, so the ribbons keep trailing the cursor.
cost: No dependencies, about 5.1 KB gzip of source, three draw calls, 150 simulated points total. Client-only and `pointer-events-none`, so it never blocks clicks, but adopting it means adding the reduced-motion check and a static frame yourself.
fit: No fit. Cursor ribbons are coloured decoration laid over the photography, and three blues would read as a second accent.
reason: playful and off-brand, and it fails the calm-static-state rule out of the box.

name: RippleDistortion-TS-TW
title: RippleDistortion
what_does: Paints a photograph into a WebGL canvas and drags its pixels sideways under the cursor, leaving a wake of decaying concentric ripples that refract the image. Optional RGB split, specular glint, tint and grayscale sit on top of the displacement.
motion: Pointer move spawns an instanced wave every 15 px, each growing then decaying on its own; a click can add a stronger one. Waves live in a 100-slot ring buffer and are drawn additively into a render target that then warps the photo. WebGL via ogl; the rAF loop runs from mount to unmount with no intersection or tab-visibility gate.
cost: ogl is roughly 20 KB gzip, plus a full-resolution image texture and DPR up to 2. Every frame costs two passes whether or not anything moved, and reduced motion only stops new waves, not the render loop. Client-only: prerender emits an empty black div, the `` and its alt text are replaced by a canvas, and `src` is fetched with `crossOrigin="anonymous"`, so it needs CORS.
fit: no fit. Photography is the argument on every page; a cursor wake that distorts it is decoration aimed at the one thing that must stay legible, and the tint defaults to violet.
reason: 20 KB of WebGL and a never-idle GPU loop to bend the photography, which is the site's argument, not its ornament.

name: RippleGrid-TS-TW
title: RippleGrid
what_does: Draws a full-bleed grid of hairlines, dots or crosshairs with a raw WebGL2 fragment shader, then bends and brightens it where waves pass through. Waves come from an interval timer, the pointer trail and clicks, and the plane can be tilted into perspective.
motion: A clock ages each wave, and every ripple pushes a Gaussian packet through the grid coordinates, so the lines visibly displace and the halo brightens. Auto waves fire every 2.6 s from the centre, a small one per ~1.6 cells of pointer travel, a 1.2-strength one per click. rAF runs whenever the canvas is on screen and unpaused, stops on intersection exit and hidden tabs; reduced motion advances nothing and draws one static frame.
cost: Zero dependencies, 18.7 KB of source, one fullscreen triangle and a single fragment pass at DPR ≤ 2 — cheap for a full-bleed layer, but it holds a permanent WebGL2 context and has no fallback: if the context or shader fails it returns an empty div. Client-only; prerender ships an aria-hidden canvas with nothing in it.
fit: no fit. A glowing technical grid reads as dashboard, not interiors, and its white cool-toned glow would compete with brass.
reason: a decorative grid with no job on any of the five pages, and one more glow language competing with the single accent.

name: RotatingText-TS-TW
title: RotatingText
what_does: Cycles a list of phrases on a timer, animating each grapheme in and out with slide, 3D flip, blur, scale or drop while the container springs to the width of the text. A highlight mode wraps the phrase in a coloured block that resizes to fit the current word.
motion: Time-triggered: a timeout swaps the phrase through AnimatePresence in wait mode, each character its own motion.span on a spring or tween, exit offset from enter. Layout springs animate width; `MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"` strips the transforms so reduced motion gets a plain text swap. Exposes next / previous / jumpTo / reset through a ref.
cost: Pulls the whole motion/react runtime, ~35–40 KB gzip, for one line of text; one span per character, doubled during the overlap, plus a layout-animated parent. Client-only for the animation; SSR renders the first phrase, so prerendered HTML is correct but rotates only after hydration.
fit: home, the line under the monument wordmark — the one place a rotating phrase could go. It is still wrong there: the wordmark is carved and fixed, and a phrase that keeps flipping is the opposite of carved.
reason: the highlight block is a second accent by construction, and a full motion runtime for one changing word does not earn its place.

name: RubberSegment-TS-TW
title: RubberSegment
what_does: A segmented control whose single thumb stretches across the gap between slots and squashes into the target before settling. It is also draggable: the thumb follows the finger, rubber-bands past the ends and projects release velocity, with arrow, Home and End keys handled and a proper radiogroup.
motion: Click, keyboard or drag moves a clip-path window over a duplicated row of labels, so the active label recolours as the thumb passes under it. Springs handle dilation, landing and squash; pointer velocity is projected for flicks; reduced motion jumps the edges with no spring. Hover/click/drag triggered, needs motion/react.
cost: motion/react runtime; every item renders twice (a button plus a clipped copy inside the thumb), so labels and fonts must stay in sync. Slots are measured on mount, on resize and after fonts load, and the thumb is zero-width until that first measurement. Client-only for measurement; SSR markup is complete but thumbless until hydration.
fit: contact, the Cairo/Dubai office switch, the only either/or on the site. Two addresses read better side by side than one hidden behind a toggle, and a squashy thumb is a toy gesture in a brand this quiet.
reason: a playful control looking for a binary the site does not have, at the cost of the motion runtime.

name: Scanner-TS-TW
title: Scanner
what_does: Renders a field of fine interference bands with a WebGL2 shader, swept by a bright scan head that leaves a lit trail, finished with CRT scanlines, grain, vignette and a coloured fringe. The pointer acts as a lens that bends bands toward or away from it, and clicks send ring pings through the field.
motion: Time drives the wave distortion and the sweep; the pointer lens and ping rings add local light and a short-lived ripple. Continuous rAF while visible unless speed and sweepSpeed are both zero, plus a 2 s intro that wipes a reveal front across the frame. Reduced motion freezes wave and sweep and skips the intro, leaving one lit static frame.
cost: Zero dependencies, 18 KB of source, one fullscreen triangle and a single fragment pass at DPR ≤ 2. WebGL2 only with no fallback — a failed context leaves an empty box — and the canvas is decorative and aria-hidden, so it adds nothing to prerender. Client-only.
fit: no fit — a CRT readout belongs to a monitoring product, not a fit-out contractor, and the violet/pink defaults would break the single-accent rule on sight.
reason: sci-fi surface effect with no job on any page, and two accents in its defaults.

name: ScrambledText-TS-TW
title: ScrambledText
what_does: Splits a paragraph into characters and, when the cursor comes within a radius, makes nearby glyphs churn through `.:` before resolving into the real letter. Clicking sends a wave across the text that scrambles every glyph it crosses; lift, blur and magnify variants shove the letters physically instead.
motion: Hover proximity, click waves and a one-time decode on first intersection. Each affected glyph runs a GSAP ScrambleText tween, with duration scaled by distance; the physical variants run on a rAF that stops once energy decays. Reduced motion drops the intro and the displacement but still scrambles glyphs on hover. Needs GSAP SplitText and ScrambleTextPlugin.
cost: GSAP plus SplitText and ScrambleTextPlugin — core alone is ~25 KB gzip, plugins on top; both plugins ship in the public gsap package from 3.13. Every character becomes a span holding a hidden sizer plus an absolutely positioned glyph, and positions are re-measured by walking the offsetParent chain per character. Waits on `document.fonts.ready`, so it re-splits after webfonts land. Client-only; prerender shows the plain paragraph.
fit: no fit. Glyph decryption is a terminal trope, the wrong register for interiors, and it imposes its own mono font and 7vw margins.
reason: a hacker effect that fights both the typography and the calm the brand needs, for a heavy new plugin dependency.

name: ScrollExpand-TS-TW
title: ScrollExpand
what_does: Pins a photograph or video in a sticky stage and grows it from a small rounded plate, 42% × 58% by default, to full bleed as the section scrolls, while a centred title fades out and an optional overlay caption fades in. Crop, corner radius, inner zoom and scroll length are all numbers, so a room can open slowly.
motion: Scroll position maps through smoothstep to a clip-path inset, an image scale, and the opacity and offset of title, hint and overlay; an exponential decay filter smooths the value unless smoothing is 0. No library and no rAF once it settles. Reduced motion removes the smoothing lag but keeps the expansion, which is scroll-linked rather than a surprise.
cost: Zero dependencies, 9 KB of source, and only clip-path, transform and opacity on a handful of nodes. Each instance adds a track 2.55× the stage height plus a sticky child; the default own-scroller mode nests a scrollbar-less scroller inside the page, so use `useWindowScroll` for a page-level reel. Prerenders correctly — the start clip is baked into the class — then hydrates to real progress.
fit: home, the six-room reel: each room arrives as a framed plate and opens to full bleed, driven by window scroll. Also the head of the projects stack. Restyle: endRadius 0, no bold title, no scrim — the caption sits in bone under the frame.
reason: the clip-path expansion is the reel's missing move and costs nothing; take the mechanism, drop the scrim, bold title and rounded corners.

name: ScrollFloat-TS-TW
title: ScrollFloat
what_does: Splits a heading into words or characters and floats them into place as the heading crosses the viewport, scrubbed to scroll rather than fired once. Four louder variants flip, scatter, blur or wave the letters, with an optional shift from a start colour to the current one.
motion: A GSAP timeline is scrubbed by ScrollTrigger across the heading's passage (default start 'center bottom+=50%', end 'bottom bottom-=40%'), so the letters track the scrollbar: opacity, yPercent, scaleX/scaleY and optional per-character colour-mix. `gsap.matchMedia` gates the whole thing to no-preference; reduced motion leaves the heading as plain text. Needs GSAP and ScrollTrigger.
cost: GSAP core plus ScrollTrigger, roughly 35 KB gzip together, and one span per character — a long heading is 40+ nodes carrying will-change. One ScrollTrigger per heading, re-measured on refresh; no rAF while idle. Client-only behaviour, but it prerenders the full heading, so nothing is hidden before hydration.
fit: services, the five trade headings, or the about statement. It could be tuned to a 12 px rise with 0.02 stagger, but the presets that justify the library — scatter, flip, wave on 2.3× vertical stretch — are exactly the loud ones the brand cannot use.
reason: GSAP plus ScrollTrigger for a per-character rise that fifteen lines of IntersectionObserver and a CSS transition already do calmly.

name: ScrollReveal-TS-TW
title: ScrollReveal
what_does: Splits a paragraph into words, characters or lines and brings them up from a dim, slightly blurred, three-degree-rotated state to full opacity as the block climbs the viewport. In scrub mode the words are tied to the scrollbar; in enter mode the block plays once when it arrives.
motion: Scroll progress becomes a per-unit t, and each word gets opacity, translate, blur and optional colour from it; the block itself rotates from baseRotation to zero across the same trigger. GSAP and ScrollTrigger under the standard no-preference matchMedia gate, painting opacity, transform and filter only, with nothing running when idle. Reduced motion leaves the text fully opaque and unrotated.
cost: GSAP core plus ScrollTrigger, ~35 KB gzip, so it must be code-split to the routes that use it. name: ScrollStack-TS-TW
title: ScrollStack
what_does: Cards pin one under another as you scroll; each arriving card pushes the ones above it deeper, scaling, dimming and tilting them back into a deck. When the last card has covered the stack the deck holds, then releases.

No GSAP, Motion or three.js. Reduced motion kills the wheel glide and snap but keeps the scroll-linked scale and dim, so the deck still reads.

One sticky wrapper plus spacer per card; each scroll frame reads `offsetHeight` and `getBoundingClientRect` per card, fine for six rooms, not fifty. `useLayoutEffect` means the server ships a plain stack and measurements start after hydration; the dim property is only consumed by the bundled `ScrollStackItem`, so custom children need their own overlay.

title: ScrollVelocity

Requires `motion/react`; reduced motion freezes the marquee and leaves the text still.

what_does: A compact number chip with a label, value, suffix and fill bar: drag it sideways and the number scrubs, with a rubber-band past the limits and a delta bubble above the chip. A click turns it into a text field for typing an exact value.

Click or Enter opens typing, arrows step, Shift ×10, Alt ×0.1, Home/End jump. Uses Motion's `animate` and `useMotionValue`; reduced motion snaps back instead of springing.

title: ShapeBlur

Redraws only while visible and while the pointer or idle drift asks it to. Client-only; without WebGL2 the canvas stays empty and `children` still show.

title: ShapeGrid

name: ShapeWaves-TS-TW
title: ShapeWaves
what_does: A full-bleed WebGPU grid of small triangles, circles and squares whose size and tint follow a drifting noise field, so bands of the grid swell and brighten as they roll across. The intro sweeps the grid in radially with a noise warp and a small overshoot. Offscreen, hidden, paused or reduced motion renders one static frame and stops.

A full-screen shader at DPR 2, a half-res two-pass blur for the bloom, and ~13k cells of CPU wave simulation at up to four substeps a frame while ripples live. Client-only and WebGPU-only: async init, no fallback content, one flat rectangle on a browser that fails.

title: ShinyText
