cost: No npm dependency, ~41 KB of TSX source, but a WebGL2 context, two render targets and four draw passes per frame; up to a 1024 px texture. The root is `position: absolute` with a separate hit layer, so the parent must be `relative`; canvas is client-only (effects only, no SSR markup) and needs a reduced-motion static frame.
fit: no fit. A peelable sticker is a playful, tactile gag; there is no surface on home, projects, services, about or contact where a draggable vinyl decal carries the photography.
reason: a 40 KB shader toy that needs cut-out PNGs and a playful brand, neither of which ARKRETE has.

name: Strands-TS-TW
title: Strands
what_does: A full-bleed fragment shader of three spectral strands twisting inside a frosted glass orb, swelling into a smooth bulge where they meet, with refraction and rim light on the glass. It leans toward the pointer, brightens on hover and pulses on click.
motion: A continuous raf clock advances the shader; pointer move sets lean and hover, pointer down adds a pulse. All motion is WebGL2 GLSL inside one full-screen quad; no animation library.
cost: No dependency, ~25 KB of source, one full-screen fragment shader doing per-pixel ray work — fill-rate bound, so mobile GPUs pay for every pixel. Client-only: the canvas is created in an effect and the container needs an explicit height; under `prefers-reduced-motion` the clock freezes and it draws a still frame.
fit: no fit. The reference is Siri's orb: a seven-colour spectral palette and an "AI assistant" silhouette, dropped into a dark room-photography site.
reason: a second palette and a permanent GPU burn for an object that says nothing about fit-out.

name: StrokeText-TS-TW
title: StrokeText
what_does: Sets a line of text as per-character SVG outlines, animates the stroke dash so the letterforms draw themselves on, then floods the fill through a wiping clip rect. Optional dashed or dotted strokes leave the letters as line drawings, with marching ants and a drop shadow.
motion: A paused GSAP timeline draws stroke-dashoffset, then wipes the fill; `scroll` arms a one-shot ScrollTrigger at `top 82%`, `hover` replays on pointer enter, `loop` yoyos forever. With reduced motion it jumps straight to the finished state. Requires GSAP plus ScrollTrigger.
cost: `gsap` + `gsap/ScrollTrigger`, roughly 35–40 KB gzip together, plus ~15 KB of source; one inline SVG with a path per character, filter and mask defs, and a measured bounding box. Renders `role="img"` with an `aria-label`, so the line is not real heading text — pair it with a hidden `h2` or accept the SEO loss. Client-measured but SSG-safe (SSR emits a hidden svg until layout runs).
fit: services, the five-trades intro heading: brass stroke drawing on, then filling to bone, once on scroll. Nowhere else — the home wordmark must stay type, and project titles need to be selectable.
reason: one services heading, code-split with GSAP, brass-to-bone; drop it if GSAP is not already in the bundle.

name: SwarmCursor-TS-TW
title: SwarmCursor
what_does: A transparent canvas of up to 800 particles that chase the pointer as a liquid swarm, curling into eddies and pouring around any element matching `targets`. On click the swarm bursts outward, and it can gather, roam or hide when the pointer leaves.
motion: Continuous raf while the pointer is inside and the container is visible: CPU spring integration plus curl noise for every particle, a coarse 16 px signed-distance grid for hovered buttons, and one instanced WebGL2 draw. No animation library.
cost: No dependency, ~36 KB of source, up to 2000 simulated agents per frame in JS arrays — main-thread cost scales with `count`. Full-section canvas, so it only makes sense inside a `relative` block with children; client-only, and reduced motion stops the simulation and leaves one static frame.
fit: no fit. A cursor-chasing swarm is ambient noise over photography, and it duplicates the pointer the site already has.
reason: main-thread particle work for decoration that fights every calm room shot.

name: SwipeRow-TS-TW
title: SwipeRow
what_does: A list row that drags sideways to expose action buttons behind it, with rubber-band resistance and a spring snap at either end. Pull past 60% of the width and the primary action commits, the row collapses to nothing and a short haptic fires on touch.
motion: motion/react `useMotionValue` + `animate` drive the row transform and rail spread; window pointer listeners track velocity, a spring settles snap-back, and the row animates height to collapse. Reduced motion resolves opens and closes instantly. Needs `motion` and two hugeicons packages.
cost: `motion` (~30–40 KB gzip), `@hugeicons/react` and `@hugeicons/core-free-icons` (tree-shaken to one icon, but two installs), ~18 KB source. One row is cheap DOM; it is the dependencies and the pointer/velocity bookkeeping that cost. Renders on the server safely, interaction client-only.
fit: no fit. There is no list, no destructive action and no account surface anywhere on the five pages; the default red action rail is also a second accent.
reason: a mobile app pattern with no row to swipe, bought with two icon packages and motion.

name: SwipeToast-TS-TW
title: SwipeToast
what_does: A dark toast card that slides in with a title, line of description and an optional action, and burns a thin horizontal fuse along its edge to show the time left. It pauses on hover, focus or a hidden tab, and can be flicked down or swiped away to dismiss.
motion: The card enters and exits with motion/react springs and drag on the y axis; the fuse is a CSS `scaleX` keyframe animation driven through the Web Animations API so it can pause and resume. Reasons are reported as `timeout`, `swipe`, `action`, `close`, `escape` or `programmatic`; reduced motion closes instantly.
cost: `motion` plus two hugeicons packages (~30–40 KB gzip for motion, icons tree-shaken to one), ~16 KB source. Fixed or inline positioning, no portal; timers and global listeners per toast. Server-safe render, client-only behaviour.
fit: contact, after the inquiry form submits — but a card with an orange burning fuse is the wrong register; a single inline confirmation line is calmer and needs no dependency.
reason: the fuse makes a reply feel urgent, and the default orange is a second accent.

name: TargetCursor-TS-TW
title: TargetCursor
what_does: Replaces the pointer with four corner brackets and a centre dot that spring after the mouse, rotate slowly at rest and snap around whatever matches `targetSelector`. The brackets stretch to the target's box, inherit its corner radius, can read a `data-cursor-label`, and squeeze on click.
motion: A raf loop integrates damped springs (centre, half-width and half-height, corner radius, rotation, lock, press, presence) and writes transforms to four spans and a dot; it spins continuously when idle and rotates to the nearest quarter-turn when it locks. Reduced motion kills the idle spin but keeps the tracking. Needs only `react-dom` for the portal.
cost: No animation library, ~14 KB source, one fixed overlay portalled to `document.body` plus an injected `<style>` that applies `cursor: none` to the scope. Fine-pointer only — it returns null on touch, so no markup is prerendered; the overlay sits at `z-index: 2147483647` and repaints on every frame the pointer moves.
fit: no fit. Hiding the native cursor taxes every click on a site whose only job is to show rooms, and a reticle reads as a weapon sight, not a fit-out.
reason: a custom cursor is usability debt, and the bracket-and-label look is game HUD, not brass-and-bone.

name: TearTicket-TS-TW
title: TearTicket
what_does: A card shaped like a ticket with a perforated stub; grab the stub and pull and the paper stretches, tears fibre by fibre along the perforation, then the stub tumbles away under gravity. Pull too little and it springs back intact; the card tilts and parallaxes with the pointer.
motion: Pointer drag runs a small physics sim (gravity 2400, hinge and spin, spring return) while motion/react handles the tilt and parallax; each perforation bridge snaps at its own threshold and the torn fibres become SVG paths. Reduced motion tears instantly. Triggered only by grab-and-pull, or keyboard activation.
cost: `motion` (~30–40 KB gzip), ~27 KB source, a fixed-pixel layout scaled to fit, plus two SVG outlines and one clip-path per card — clip-path on a large element is GPU-composited but can be expensive while dragging. Client-only physics; no meaningful server render beyond the static card.
fit: no fit. Tearing a perforated stub is a ticket-and-coupon metaphor; on an interiors site it reads as a promotion, and a fixed 460×250 card fights the full-bleed room photography.
reason: a very good paper trick looking for a ticketing product, not a fit-out portfolio.

name: TechText-TS-TW
title: TechText
what_does: Draws a wordmark on a 2D canvas where letters near the pointer dissolve into dashed vector outlines and back, with optional selection handles, dimension ticks and drifting specks. Letters can be dragged and settle with a bounce, and the intro can type, assemble or draw measurement guides.
motion: Continuous 2D canvas repaint while the pointer is inside: a lens region converts covered pixels into cached per-glyph dashed sprites, plus spring-settled drag and an optional intro. No WebGL, no animation library; reduced motion draws once and stays still.
cost: No dependency, ~38 KB source, one canvas plus an offscreen sprite canvas per glyph at DPR — real memory and repaint cost on a large wordmark. Renders `role="img"` with `aria-label`, so the text is a picture: it cannot be the `h1`, cannot be selected and gives crawlers no heading.
fit: no fit. The home monument wordmark must stay real type in bone ink; the dashed-path, tick-label, selection-handle language is exactly the blueprint/mono-label look the brand rules out.
reason: a canvas wordmark that turns the one piece of type the site is built around into an image with tool chrome.

name: TextCursor-TS-TW
title: TextCursor
what_does: Stamps copies of a word or emoji along the path the pointer travels, each turned to the direction of travel and shrinking and fading behind the head. `stamp` drops a copy every `spacing` pixels, `chain` keeps a fixed tail of copies alive, `ribbon` lays the word's individual letters along the trail.
motion: Pointer-driven rAF loop: copies pop in, rotate to the path heading, optionally drift, then scale down and fade on a removal timer; the loop parks once the tail is empty. No library. `prefers-reduced-motion` kills the pop and float but keeps the stamping.
cost: No dependencies, ~14 KB source / ~4 KB gzip. One absolutely positioned span per stamp, recycled through a pool, plus a pruned path array; transform and opacity written per element per frame. Server render is an empty layer, so no hydration mismatch, but the trail is client-only.
fit: no fit. The home hero is a logo lockup over photography and a text trail there competes with the room; no other section of the five pages has a free cursor surface.
reason: decoration with no job, and the only reusable part is the pointer-path maths.

name: TextLoop-TS-TW
title: TextLoop
what_does: Repeats a string along an SVG path — wave, circle, infinity, arch, line, or your own path data — and slides it continuously, with an optional solid ribbon strip under the letters and an optional second path crossing it. Both ends are masked to fade out.
motion: Time-driven offset along the path, advanced by `gsap.ticker`; only runs while the SVG is in view. Hover eases the base speed to zero, drag release throws a fling, and `scrollBoost` adds scroll velocity. Reduced motion sets base speed to 0 and never starts the ticker, leaving static text on the path.
cost: GSAP is the only dependency and the site has none, so this brings ~23 KB gzip for a ticker and one hover tween. SVG `textPath` with the string repeated to fill the path; the first server render is one repetition, then measurement after fonts load reflows it to N. IntersectionObserver stops it offscreen.
fit: no fit. A perpetual marquee is the one kind of motion the design deliberately avoids, and the default violet ribbon is a second accent.
reason: 23 KB of GSAP to run a ticker, for a strip the pages have no place for.

name: TextPressure-TS-TW
title: TextPressure
what_does: Splits a headline into one span per character and pushes each character's variable-font axes — weight 100–1000, width 5–205, italic, alpha — by how close the pointer is, so letters swell and thicken as you pass. Optional idle wave or pulse and a click ripple that travels through the line.
motion: Pointer proximity measured per glyph on every rAF frame; the loop parks after about 60 idle frames. Idle wave/pulse only run while the pointer is outside. No library — but it needs a variable font, and the default pulls Roboto Flex from Google Fonts at runtime.
cost: No JS dependencies, ~13 KB source / ~4 KB gzip. One span per character and a `getBoundingClientRect` for every character on every running frame, so long headlines cause layout work. Adds a remote stylesheet and font file (third-party connection, FOUT) and bakes `uppercase` into the `h1`. Prerenders at `minFontSize` then resizes after hydration.
fit: no fit. The hero is an SVG wordmark, every other heading is sentence case, and a headline that warps under the cursor fights the calm the brand is built on.
reason: needs an external variable font and an uppercase text heading the site doesn't have.

name: TextType-TS-TW
title: TextType
what_does: Types one or more sentences character by character behind a blinking caret, pauses, deletes and moves to the next. It can plant deliberate typos and animate each new character with a fade, blur or rise.
motion: A `setTimeout` cadence per character, not a frame loop; GSAP drives the caret blink and its glide from the end of one line to the start of the next. `startOnVisible` uses an IntersectionObserver. Reduced motion sets the whole string at once and kills the blink and the character effects.
cost: GSAP is a hard dependency and is used only for a blinking caret and a small glide — ~23 KB gzip for two tweens on a site that has no GSAP. One span per visible character plus the caret; the full sentence is duplicated in an sr-only span so prerender and crawlers get it. Effectively client-only.
fit: no fit. Every heading is a fixed statement, and the one place copy appears in response to an action — the contact confirmation — has to be instant.
reason: a typewriter delays reading and drags in GSAP for a caret.

name: ThoughtLine-TS-TW
title: ThoughtLine
what_does: An AI "thinking" status line: glyph, label and a live timer that expands into a list of steps, ticks them off as they finish, then folds into one line reading "Thought for 3.2s". Steps cross-fade in and dim when done.
motion: motion/react loops a breathing opacity on label and glyph and animates height/opacity on settle; a CSS keyframe pulses unfinished step dots and a shimmer sweeps the label. `useReducedMotion` damps the breath and drops the shimmer. Click toggles the trace.
cost: motion plus two Hugeicons packages for three glyphs; ~14 KB source / 3.8 KB gzip before those. A live timer re-renders every 100 ms, and an `aria-live` region announces the label. Client-only by nature.
fit: no fit. There is no assistant, agent or asynchronous process on the site to narrate; a "Thinking…" row on an interior fit-out page is nonsense.
reason: an AI chat primitive with no surface here.

name: Threads-TS-TW
title: Threads
what_does: Fills its box with a WebGL2 canvas of fine parallel lines — 90 by default — that flow, fray into separate strands and part around the pointer, lit like silk or contour lines. Colour can shift toward an accent near the cursor.
motion: Continuous time-driven vertex shader (Perlin displacement) with a pointer-eased parting field, rendered in two passes: instanced line strips into an FBO, then a tone-mapped full-screen quad. rAF stops offscreen and on hidden tabs. Reduced motion freezes time, leaving one static frame.
cost: No dependencies, ~20 KB source / 5.7 KB gzip with shaders inline. One canvas, one offscreen pass, 90 instanced strips at up to 2× DPR — continuous GPU load while visible, and it will show on phones. Server render is an empty div.
fit: no fit. Every section already carries a photograph; an abstract line field behind it is decoration with a real GPU bill.
reason: good-looking and unemployed, and a permanent WebGL loop is the wrong cost for this page weight.

name: TiltedCard-TS-TW
title: TiltedCard
what_does: A card that rotates in 3D toward the pointer with a moving glare, a soft ground shadow and inner layers that parallax at different depths. An optional back face flips into place on click or Enter.
motion: `pointermove` feeds an eased rAF that writes rotateX/rotateY and translates each layer by its depth; the flip is a 180° rotateY with a spring settle; optional intro rise. Reduced motion cuts tilt to 30%, drops the intro and float, and flips instantly. No library.
cost: No dependencies, ~25 KB source / 6.7 KB gzip. Five-plus absolutely positioned layers per face, two radial-gradient overlays and a masked rim, `preserve-3d` and backface hiding; rAF only while moving or settling. SSR-safe markup, interaction client-only.
fit: no fit. Projects are a full-bleed scroll stack and services a flex accordion; a tilting card with glare belongs to a product grid the site never uses.
reason: strong for a shop, the wrong idiom for full-bleed rooms.

name: Topography-TS-TW
title: Topography
what_does: Draws a 3D landscape in glowing contour lines that drifts under a tilted camera, rises where the pointer rests and sends a ring across the terrain on click. Optional plus or dot markers sit on the surface.
motion: A WebGL2 grid terrain with contour lines shaded in the fragment shader: noise drifts with time, the pointer sculpts a height texture, clicks add pulse rings, and an optional intro raises the land. Camera leans with the pointer. Pauses offscreen and when the tab is hidden; reduced motion skips intro, parallax and glitch but keeps the drift.
cost: No dependencies, but ~58 KB source / ~15 KB gzip of inline GLSL — the heaviest file in the batch. Four bloom levels, float targets where available, up to 200k cells per rebuild, DPR capped at 2. A full-screen WebGL loop that will dominate a mid-range phone; server render is an empty canvas.
fit: no fit. A glowing abstract terrain has no job next to room photography, and its default blue is a second accent.
reason: the most expensive thing here and the furthest from the brand.

name: TrueFocus-TS-TW
title: TrueFocus
what_does: Splits a sentence into words, keeps one sharp and blurs the rest, and walks a bracket, box, underline or highlight frame from word to word on a timer. Hovering a word takes over when `manualMode` is on.
motion: A `setInterval` advances the active word; motion/react springs or eases the frame rectangle while CSS transitions filter, opacity and scale on every word. Reduced motion sets duration to 0 and drops the spring, so the frame jumps.
cost: motion for the frame; ~8 KB source / 2.5 KB gzip plus the runtime. A blur filter on each word creates a composited layer per word, sizes are hardcoded at `3rem font-black`, so it only works as display type. The prerendered HTML shows the sentence blurred around word one until hydration.
fit: no fit. The site never shows one word of a sentence at a time, and a camera-focus bracket is a metaphor with no meaning for a fit-out firm; the default green is a second accent.
reason: a hero gadget that hides copy and adds a motion runtime for a frame.

name: VariableProximity-TS-TW
title: VariableProximity
what_does: Splits a line of text into single-letter spans and drives each letter's variable-font axes from its distance to the cursor, so weight and optical size swell under the pointer and settle back as it leaves. An optional idle wave rolls the same swell across the line on a loop, and line breaks are re-measured so the effect survives wrapping.
motion: Per-letter `font-variation-settings` (and optional colour and transform) are written in a RAF loop, eased toward pointer-derived targets; the loop only runs while letters are settling or the idle wave is on. Triggered by window-level `mousemove`/`touchmove`, scroll, and font load; no animation library, but it needs a variable font with the named axes.
cost: Zero npm dependencies, about 15 KB source (~5 KB gzip), but it injects a Google Fonts `@import` for Roboto Flex and hardcodes that family, so it brings a second typeface. One span per letter plus a `getBoundingClientRect` per letter on pointer frames, and a full re-measure on resize/font load; the markup prerenders, the interaction is client-only.
fit: No fit. The home monument is an SVG `Logo`, not text, and every heading is set in the site's Archivo/Schibsted faces; swapping in Roboto Flex to make letters breathe under the cursor adds a second typographic voice for a hover flourish.
reason: needs Roboto Flex and per-letter hit-testing for a hover effect that fights the monument wordmark.

name: VoicePill-TS-TW
title: VoicePill
what_does: A 28 px mic button that opens into a capsule with a live canvas equalizer and a running timer while recording; drag left past 64 px to cancel, release to stop. With `reactive="mic"` it reads the real microphone through an `AnalyserNode`, otherwise it plays a canned syllable envelope.
motion: The capsule's background clip-path opens leftward over 200 ms; the mic icon blurs and scales into a stop square; a 2D canvas draws an 80-sample scrolling equalizer at 60 fps while recording; dragging translates the pill and fades in a "Cancel" row. CSS transitions plus a RAF canvas, no animation library.
cost: Two Hugeicons packages, tree-shaken down to the mic and arrow icons, about 19 KB source (~6 KB gzip), canvas and RAF only while recording, plus `AudioContext` and a `getUserMedia` permission prompt in mic mode. Client-only: pointer capture, audio hardware, and a permission gate.
fit: No fit. The contact form is a written inquiry; a mic permission prompt is a trust cost on a contractor's page and there is no voice-note pipeline behind it.
reason: a voice-recording affordance with no job on a typed inquiry form.

name: WakeSlider-TS-TW
title: WakeSlider
what_does: A thumbless range slider drawn as 32 thin vertical bars: filled bars light up to the value, and the bar tops lift in a travelling wake whose height follows drag velocity, then settle. It is a real control — pointer drag, click-to-seek, arrow/Page/Home/End keys, and ARIA slider attributes.
motion: The handle position is a `useSpring` on the value, with a second spring on its velocity; bar `scaleY` and crest opacity are painted per frame from both, so the wake leads or trails the handle by `skew` and decays with `glide`/`smoothing`. Drag, click, and keyboard trigger it; needs `motion` (the Framer Motion successor).
cost: `motion@^12` adds the motion runtime (tens of KB gzip depending on tree-shaking), about 9 KB component source; 32 spans transformed per frame while moving, no canvas. Reduced motion renders a flat fill and no springs. Prerenders its bars, but the interaction and springs are client-only.
fit: No fit. The site has no numeric control anywhere — no budget slider, no stat row, no configurator — so the control has no question to answer.
reason: a nicely made slider for a site that never asks for a number.

name: WarmTooltip-TS-TW
title: WarmTooltip
what_does: A tooltip group where the first label waits 400 ms, then sibling labels open instantly while the group is "warm" and the tooltip springs from one trigger to the next. Labels portal to the body, follow their trigger on scroll, and can show a keyboard-shortcut chip.
motion: Cold opens pop from 0.94 scale with a 4 px blur over 160 ms; warm swaps slide 10 px and blur out the old label; the whole plate travels between triggers on a 320 ms spring with the arrow tracking the anchor, and optional `lean` rotates it with pointer velocity. Hover, focus, touch long-press, and Escape; needs `motion` plus a react-dom portal.
cost: `motion@^12` plus react-dom, about 25 KB source (~7 KB gzip before the motion runtime); one portal node and a global scroll/resize listener while open, plus per-trigger timers. Trigger markup prerenders; the overlay is client-only.
fit: No fit. Header and footer are text links with visible labels, and hiding an office address behind hover on contact would cost the reader a discovery rather than save space.
reason: a motion-heavy tooltip system for a site with no icon-only controls.

name: WarpText-TS-TW
title: WarpText
what_does: Rasterises a headline to an offscreen canvas, uploads it as a WebGL texture, and warps it with fbm noise and a pointer lens, adding refraction and optional chromatic split; clicks send shockwave rings through the letters. The raster is re-cut on resize, font load, and colour change so the type stays sharp.
motion: Pointer move bends and refracts the texture around a lens; fbm drift keeps it alive when idle; clicks spawn up to four ripple rings; the intro reveals the text over 1.6 s. Needs WebGL2 through `ogl` and a continuous RAF while the canvas is in view; reduced motion freezes time and dampens the pointer.
cost: `ogl@^1.0.11` (~8 KB gzip), about 25 KB source, a full-viewport fragment shader with seven texture taps per pixel and a canvas raster per resize; one WebGL context per instance. Client-only: prerender emits an empty `div` with an `aria-label`, and text is an image, not selectable.
fit: No fit. The home monument is a fixed SVG wordmark and section titles are plain text; turning either into a shader texture would make the strongest typographic asset unselectable and soft.
reason: a WebGL text toy that spends a context and a hero on decoration.

name: Waves-TS-TW
title: Waves
what_does: Draws dense silk-like lines that undulate with Perlin noise, part around the cursor, and spring back when it leaves; clicks send a radial ripple through the strands. Solid or dashed lines, rotation, spacing, fade and a light-mode ink treatment are exposed.
motion: A vertex shader waves each strand; a CPU spring grid (12 px cells, simulated only inside the pointer's dirty rectangle) displaces it near the cursor and on click, while the noise field flows continuously. Raw WebGL2, no animation library; the RAF stops when off-screen or fully settled.
cost: Zero dependencies, about 26 KB source (~8 KB gzip), one WebGL2 context, an instanced draw capped at 1.6 M vertices, and a JS spring loop over the active grid area per frame. Client-only; no WebGL2 or no JS leaves only the background colour.
fit: No fit. Home and project pages are carried by full-bleed photography, and a generative line field behind them is a competing texture with no informational job.
reason: beautiful silk lines that would put a second, abstract world behind the photographs.

name: WebThreads-TS-TW
title: WebThreads
what_does: A full-screen shader weaving up to 24 glowing threads that pinch through one or more nodes; the strand nearest the cursor brightens while the others dim, and a click sends a light surge along the bundle. Palette, pinch point, node count, angle and grain are all props.
motion: Threads undulate and shimmer with time; hover runs a CPU distance test against each strand, then eases focus and dims the rest; click fires a travelling surge; intro strokes the bundle in. Requires WebGL2, no library; after three quiet frames it stops re-rendering, though the RAF keeps ticking.
cost: Zero dependencies, about 24 KB source (~7 KB gzip), a full-screen fragment shader looping over up to 24 threads per pixel, one canvas and RAF while visible, DPR capped at 2 by default. Client-only; without WebGL2 it renders an empty transparent div.
fit: No fit. Luminous neon threads read as a crypto or AI-studio motif, not plaster, stone and joinery, and no ARKRETE section needs a glowing backdrop.
reason: a striking tech-brand background with nothing to say about interior fit-out.
